The new image is opened and verified via `verify_integrity()` (fsck) ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L570-L578)). ### 6. Atomic commit or rollback On success: the `.old` backup is deleted and the active `DiskManager` handle **live-reloads** via `reload_from_disk()` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L580-L586)), synchronizing its in-memory state (superblock, bitmaps, caches, hints) with the new file. On any failure: the `.old` backup is renamed back to the original path, restoring the pre-defrag state ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L588-L597)). ## In-place defragmentation (WAL-atomic COW) [`defragment_inplace_on`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L643-L735) performs defragmentation directly within the existing image file. Two implementations exist: ### Legacy non-journaled path (`defragment_inplace_legacy`) Used when the image has no journal layout. It performs a **cycle-aware block permutation**: 1. **Target computation**: All allocated blocks (directory payload, file payload, indirect blocks, `ChunkEntry` runs) are assigned contiguous target locations starting at `data_block_start` ([`defragment_inplace_legacy`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L737-L818)). 2. **Cycle resolution**: A `pending` map tracks `old_block → new_block`. Blocks whose targets are already free are moved directly. Cycles are broken by copying the cycle leader to a scratch buffer, rotating the cycle, then writing the scratch buffer to the final destination ([`defragment_inplace_legacy`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L820-L870)). 3. **Metadata update**: Inode pointers, indirect block pointers, and `ChunkEntry` values are rewritten using the `old_to_new` mapping ([`defragment_inplace_legacy`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L872-L910)). 4. **Bitmap rebuild**: The data bitmap is reset and `set_range(0, total_used)` marks the new contiguous allocation ([`defragment_inplace_legacy`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L912-L918)). 5. **Sync**: Metadata ranges are flushed according to `DurabilityMode` ([`defragment_inplace_legacy`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L920-L926)). ### WAL-atomic round-based COW (`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`) Used when the image has a journal layout (`superblock.has_journal_layout()`). This is the **only path that runs under the auto-defrag coordinator** on journaled images. It operates in **rounds**, each committing a single bounded WAL transaction: ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Round Start] --> B{Select relocatable
units with free targets
and WAL budget} B -->|None free| C[Cycle breaker:
move 1 unit to
high free run] B -->|Some free| D[Copy payload blocks
to free destinations] C --> D D --> E[Strict mode?
flush dest ranges] E --> F[Stage metadata ops:
inode ptrs, indirect slots,
ChunkEntry rewrites,
bitmap alloc/free] F --> G[Commit single bounded
WAL transaction] G --> H[apply_journal_ops
in-place] H --> I[Update in-memory
alloc bitmap mirror] I --> J[Sync metadata per
DurabilityMode] J --> K[Checkpoint WAL ring] K --> L{More units?} L -->|Yes| A L -->|No| M[Update hints,
remap dir cache] ``` **Detailed round steps** ([`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L928-L1400)): 1. **Unit collection**: All relocatable units are discovered—direct blocks, indirect blocks (SIB/DIB/TIB), and `ChunkEntry` runs—with ownership metadata (`UnitOwner` enum) tracking which inode slot or indirect slot owns each unit. Target locations are assigned sequentially from `data_block_start` ([`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L930-L1030)). 2. **Free-target selection**: Each round greedily selects units whose target ranges are **currently free** in the in-memory allocation bitmap mirror (`alloc_bm_bytes`) and whose estimated WAL transaction fits within **half the journal ring** (`max_payload_per_tx`) ([`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1035-L1080)). 3. **Cycle breaker**: If no unit has a free target, the smallest unit is moved to a high-address free run found by scanning the allocation bitmap backwards ([`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1082-L1095)). 4. **Payload copy**: Selected units' blocks are copied to their free destinations via `backing.copy_block`. In `DurabilityMode::Strict`, destination ranges are flushed before WAL commit ([`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1097-L1115)). 5. **WAL staging**: Metadata operations are staged into `wal_ops`: - Inode pointer updates (`WriteInode` ops) - Indirect block slot updates (`WriteBlockSlice` ops) - `ChunkEntry` rewrites (packed into inode slots or indirect slots) - Data bitmap range alloc/free (`SetDataBitmapRange` ops) Operations are coalesced to minimize WAL size ([`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1117-L1195)). 6. **Commit & apply**: `commit_journal_tx` writes the transaction; `apply_journal_ops` applies metadata updates in-place using the exact same op applier used during journal recovery ([`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1197-L1205)). 7. **State advance**: The in-memory allocation bitmap mirror is updated (clear old, set new). `ChunkEntry` values and indirect block indices in `units` are rewritten to their new locations ([`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1207-L1225)). 8. **Metadata sync & WAL checkpoint**: Modified metadata ranges (data bitmap, inodes, indirect blocks, destination payloads in range-based modes) are synced per `DurabilityMode`. The WAL ring is checkpointed (`ring.checkpoint()`) so the next round reuses the freed source blocks ([`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1227-L1255)). ### Seekable 64K chunked file handling Both in-place paths correctly handle **seekable 64K chunked files** (`INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K`). Their inode pointer slots hold packed `ChunkEntry` values (u64 encoding `start_block`, `block_count`, `flags`, `compressed_len`) instead of raw block IDs. The `collect_inode_block_layout` helper expands `ChunkEntry` runs into individual block IDs for bitmap analysis, while the defragmentation logic rewrites the packed `ChunkEntry` with the new `start_block` ([`collect_inode_block_layout`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L257-L320), [`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1145-L1155)). ## Auto-defragmentation coordinator The [`AutoDefragController`](repo://src/auto_defrag.rs#L235-L320) runs a **daemon thread** named `oifs-auto-defrag` that holds a `Weak>` reference to the `DiskManager` inner state. This ensures the worker exits as soon as the last `DiskManager` clone is dropped, never keeping the image mapped indefinitely. ### Configuration [`AutoDefragConfig`](repo://src/auto_defrag.rs#L25-L80) controls the coordinator: | Field | Default | Purpose | |-------|---------|---------| | `enabled` | `false` | Opt-in activation | | `fragmentation_threshold` | `0.25` | Ratio above which a pass triggers (clamped to `[0,1]`, NaN → default) | | `check_interval` | `300s` | Measurement period (min `10ms`, prevents hot loop) | | `min_free_blocks` | `0` | Minimum free blocks required to run (guards near-full images) | | `allow_journaled` | `true` | Permit in-place defrag on WAL-enabled images | The configuration is **sanitized on install** (`AutoDefragConfig::sanitized`): NaN thresholds are replaced, intervals below `MIN_CHECK_INTERVAL` are raised, and the threshold is clamped ([`auto_defrag.rs`](repo://src/auto_defrag.rs#L60-L78)). ### Worker loop The worker ([`run_worker`](repo://src/auto_defrag.rs#L330-L385)): 1. Sleeps on a `Condvar` with timeout = `check_interval`, waking early on config change or shutdown. 2. Upgrades the `Weak` reference; exits if the manager is gone. 3. Takes a **read lock** and calls `analyze_fragmentation_on` to measure fragmentation. 4. Evaluates skip conditions via `skip_reason`: - Fragmentation ratio below threshold - Free blocks below `min_free_blocks` - Journaled image with `allow_journaled = false` 5. If not skipped, takes a **write lock** and runs `defragment_inplace_on` (which selects the WAL-atomic path on journaled images). 6. Updates statistics under `stats` mutex. ### Statistics [`AutoDefragStats`](repo://src/auto_defrag.rs#L82-L95) tracks: - `checks`: Total fragmentation measurements - `passes`: Successful defragmentation passes - `skipped`: Passes skipped (with reason in `last_error`) - `errors`: Failed passes (with error in `last_error`) - `last_fragmentation_ratio`: Most recent measurement - `last_pass`: `Option` from the last successful pass - `last_error`: Human-readable skip/failure reason ### Lifecycle integration - `DiskManager::set_auto_defrag(config)` installs sanitized config and starts/stops the worker ([`disk.rs`](repo://src/disk.rs)). - `DiskManager::stop_auto_defrag()` and `AutoDefragController::shutdown()` stop the worker; the latter is called from `DiskManager::drop` ([`auto_defrag.rs`](repo://src/auto_defrag.rs#L285-L315)). ## Key invariants and failure semantics | Invariant | Enforcement | |-----------|-------------| | **Original image untouched until commit** | Safe mode copies entire image first; InPlace only modifies after WAL commit | | **Atomic metadata updates** | InPlace: single WAL transaction per round; Safe: full fsck before rename | | **No metadata corruption on crash** | Safe: rollback via `.old` rename; InPlace: WAL orders payload before metadata | | **Live handle consistency** | Safe: `reload_from_disk()` after swap; InPlace: operates under write lock on live handle | | **Worker never leaks manager** | `Weak` reference + `shutdown()` on `Drop` | | **No hot loop** | `MIN_CHECK_INTERVAL = 10ms` enforced in config sanitization | ## Extension points - **Custom defrag modes**: Add variants to `DefragMode` and dispatch in `defragment()`. - **Allocation policy**: The contiguous allocator (`allocate_contiguous_blocks`) is used by both safe and in-place paths; modifying it changes placement strategy. - **Auto-defrag policy**: `skip_reason` is a pure function; alternative policies (time-of-day, IO load) can be injected by wrapping the controller. - **ChunkEntry compaction**: The `shift_table_collapse` logic (used during file truncate/rewrite) is separate from defragmentation but shares `ChunkEntry` rewrite mechanics. ## Configuration and operations ```rust // Enable auto-defrag with default threshold (0.25), checking every 60s dm.set_auto_defrag(AutoDefragConfig::new(0.25).with_check_interval(Duration::from_secs(60))); // Disable auto-defrag dm.set_auto_defrag(AutoDefragConfig::default()); // Read stats let stats = dm.auto_defrag_stats(); println!("checks={}, passes={}, skipped={}, errors={}", stats.checks, stats.passes, stats.skipped, stats.errors); // Manual defrag let stats = dm.defragment(&path, DefragMode::Safe, None)?; // or let stats = dm.defragment(&path, DefragMode::InPlace, None)?; ``` ## Focused tests | Test file | Coverage | |-----------|----------| | `tests/defrag_test.rs` | Safe & in-place defrag, encrypted images, indirect files, path injection defense, live reload | | `tests/defrag_seekable_chunk_test.rs` | Seekable 64K chunked file preservation in both defrag modes | | `tests/auto_defrag_test.rs` | Config sanitization (NaN, zero interval), disabled default, pass execution, data integrity, journaled images, `allow_journaled=false`, `min_free_blocks`, shutdown on disable |

nodes.title: DiskManager & Persistence
nodes.description: Central coordinator for OIFS storage: image open/create, superblock management, inode CRUD, data read/write with compression/encryption, durability modes, flush/msync, read-only mounts, and atomic rename.
nodes.body:
# DiskManager & Persistence [`DiskManager`](../../src/disk.rs#L324-L327) is the central coordinator of the OIFS storage engine. It provides the single authoritative interface between raw on-disk bytes and high-level filesystem operations (file and directory creation, reads, writes, deletion, path resolution, defragmentation, and integrity checks). ## DiskManagerInner State Internally, state is maintained by `DiskManagerInner` ([`src/disk.rs#L191-L213`](../../src/disk.rs#L191-L213)), wrapped in an `Arc>` ([`src/disk.rs#L324-L327`](../../src/disk.rs#L324-L327)): - **`file`**: The underlying host image file handle with an exclusive POSIX advisory lock (`F_SETLK` for read-write, `F_RDLCK` for read-only). - **`backing`**: The active storage engine (`ImageBacking`) supporting `Mmap` (shared `PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE`), `MmapReadOnly` (shared `PROT_READ`), `Pread`, and `IoUring` backends. - **`superblock`**: In-memory cached copy of the deserialized `SuperBlock` ([`src/superblock.rs`](../../src/superblock.rs)). - **`encryption_key`**: Derived cryptographic key (`Option`) used for authenticated AEAD encryption. - **`password_verifier`**: Keyed BLAKE2b verifier of the mount password for session re-authentication. - **`free_block_hint`** and **`free_inode_hint`**: Allocation watermarks that convert sequential bitmap scans into amortized $O(1)$ operations. - **`inode_cache`**: In-memory zero-copy cache (`RwLock`) avoiding redundant bincode deserialization. - **`dir_cache`**: Sharded per-directory name index (`ShardedDirCache`) providing $O(1)$ path queries. - **`chunk_read_cache`**: `RwLock` — bounded sub-chunk decompression cache for seekable 64K `read_at`. - **`decoded_blob_cache`**: `Mutex` — bounded decoded-payload cache for non-seekable `read_at` (compressed/encrypted files ≤ 16 MiB). - **`durability_mode`**: `AtomicU8` durability policy governing `msync` flush behavior on writes. - **`pending_async_ranges`**: `Mutex` — batched dirty-range accumulator for `DurabilityMode::RangeAsync`. - **`async_drain_ready`**: `Arc` — fast atomic flag set when `pending_async_ranges` reaches its drain threshold. - **`io_engine`**: Pluggable data-block read engine supporting `Mmap`, `Pread`, and Linux `io_uring` backends. - **`inode_write_gen`**: Per-inode write generation counters (indexed by `inode_id & 4095`) for lock-free Stage-1 → Stage-3 staleness detection. - **`read_only`**: `bool` — strictly read-only mount (`F_RDLCK`, zero disk writes). ## Architecture Overview ```text flowchart TB subgraph DM[DiskManager] inner[Arc>] sync_mutex[Arc>] async_drain[Arc] auto_defrag[AutoDefragController] end subgraph Inner[DiskManagerInner] file[(File Handle)] backing[ImageBacking] sb[SuperBlock] enc_key[EncryptionKey?] pwd_verifier[PasswordVerifier?] free_blk_hint[u64] free_ino_hint[u64] inode_cache[BoundedInodeCache] dir_cache[ShardedDirCache] chunk_cache[ChunkReadCache] blob_cache[DecodedBlobCache] durability[AtomicU8] pending_ranges[PendingAsyncRanges] async_drain_ready[Arc] io_engine[IoEngine] inode_write_gen[Box<[u64;4096]>] read_only[bool] end subgraph IO[Pluggable I/O Engines] mmap[Mmap] pread[Pread] iouring[IoUring] end inner --> Inner Inner --> file Inner --> backing Inner --> sb Inner --> enc_key Inner --> pwd_verifier Inner --> free_blk_hint Inner --> free_ino_hint Inner --> inode_cache Inner --> dir_cache Inner --> chunk_cache Inner --> blob_cache Inner --> durability Inner --> pending_ranges Inner --> async_drain_ready Inner --> io_engine Inner --> inode_write_gen Inner --> read_only io_engine --> mmap io_engine --> pread io_engine --> iouring sync_mutex -.->|serializes msync| Inner async_drain -.->|signals drain| pending_ranges ``` ## Lifecycle, Image Locking, and Initialization `DiskManager` instances are constructed via factory methods that all delegate to the unified `init_or_open_with_key` routine ([`src/disk.rs#L1475-L1550`](../../src/disk.rs#L1475-L1550)): ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Factory[Factory Methods] new[new/create] open[open] open_ro[open_read_only*] open_ro_pwd[open_read_only_with_password] open_ro_sm[open_read_only_with_storage_mode] end subgraph Core[init_or_open_with_key] lock[F_SETLK / F_RDLCK] mmap[Mmap or FileIo] sb[SuperBlock] enc[Encryption Key] jrnl[Journal Recovery] init[Inner State] end Factory --> Core Core --> lock lock --> mmap mmap --> sb sb --> enc enc --> jrnl jrnl --> init ``` ### Read-Write Mount (`new`, `open`, `open_with_password`) 1. Open the image file with `O_RDWR|O_CREAT` (no `O_TRUNC` before locking). 2. Acquire an **exclusive non-blocking advisory lock** (`fcntl(F_SETLK, F_WRLCK)` on the whole file). This prevents concurrent read-write mounts and read-only mounts. 3. If the file is new/empty/truncated, create a fresh `SuperBlock` (journaled or legacy layout), generate encryption salt/key if requested, serialize and write block 0. 4. If the file exists, read and validate the superblock (magic, bounds, geometry). 5. Load bitmap mirrors and journal mirrors for `FileIo` mode. 6. **Mount-time journal recovery**: On journaled images, replay all durable-but-unapplied transactions from the WAL ring **before** the manager is published. This ensures no caller ever observes a filesystem mid-replay. 7. If newly created, allocate root inode (0) and root data block; write root inode; flush. 8. If existing, mark journal clean (write a clean-shutdown marker) for fast future mounts. ### Read-Only Mount (`open_read_only*`) 1. Open the image file with `O_RDONLY` (succeeds on `0444` files). 2. Acquire a **shared non-blocking advisory lock** (`fcntl(F_SETLK, F_RDLCK)`). Multiple read-only processes can coexist; a read-write mount (`F_WRLCK`) is rejected. 3. Map the image `PROT_READ` (`MmapReadOnly` backing) — full zero-copy read support. 4. Read and validate superblock; derive encryption key if encrypted. 5. **Journal cleanliness check**: Verify with **zero disk writes** that the WAL ring contains `0` unrecovered transactions. If `pending_txs > 0`, reject the mount and instruct the user to open read-write first to recover. 6. Initialize inner state with `read_only = true`; `Drop` performs **no flushes**. ### Locking Guarantees | Mount Type | File Mode | Advisory Lock | Allows Concurrent | Blocks | |------------|-----------|---------------|-------------------|--------| | Read-Write | `O_RDWR` | `F_WRLCK` (exclusive) | — | All other mounts | | Read-Only | `O_RDONLY`| `F_RDLCK` (shared) | Other read-only | Read-write | The lock is held for the lifetime of the `DiskManager` and released on `Drop`. ## Durability Modes `DurabilityMode` ([`src/disk.rs#L210-L232`](../../src/disk.rs#L210-L232)) controls when and how `msync` is called on the backing memory map. Shared memory mappings (`MAP_SHARED`) write directly to the OS page cache, ensuring modifications survive application process crashes (e.g. `SIGKILL`). Policies balance power-loss resilience against write throughput. ```text flowchart TD subgraph Modes[DurabilityMode enum] Lazy[Lazy = 0
default] RangeAsync[RangeAsync = 1] Strict[Strict = 2] Legacy[LegacyWholeMmapAsync = 3] end subgraph Behavior[Flush Behavior] L1[No per-mutation msync] L2[Survives process crash] L3[Power-loss: explicit flush/Drop/OS writeback] R1[msync(MS_ASYNC) on modified byte ranges] R2[Batched outside write lock] R3[Coalesced with 1 MB gap bridging] S1[msync(MS_SYNC) on modified byte ranges] S2[Synchronous; data on physical media before return] S3[Coalesced with 256 KB gap bridging] W1[msync(MS_ASYNC) on ENTIRE mmap] W2[Legacy whole-mapping flush] end Lazy --> L1 Lazy --> L2 Lazy --> L3 RangeAsync --> R1 RangeAsync --> R2 RangeAsync --> R3 Strict --> S1 Strict --> S2 Strict --> S3 Legacy --> W1 Legacy --> W2 ``` ### Detailed Semantics | Mode | Value | Per-Mutation Flush | Syscall | Scope | Ordering Guarantees | |------|-------|-------------------|---------|-------|---------------------| | **Lazy** | 0 (default) | None | — | — | Process-crash safe (page cache). Power-loss safe only on explicit `flush()`, `Drop`, or kernel writeback. Up to ~45× faster bulk write throughput. | | **RangeAsync** | 1 | Async | `msync(MS_ASYNC)` | Modified byte ranges only, coalesced, 1 MB gap bridging | Accumulated in `pending_async_ranges`, drained in batches (64 ops / 4 MiB / 256 ranges) **outside** the exclusive write lock via background thread or inline fallback. Journal region flushed first to preserve WAL-before-metadata ordering. | | **Strict** | 2 | Sync | `msync(MS_SYNC)` | Modified byte ranges only, coalesced, 256 KB gap bridging | Data reaches physical storage before the mutating function returns. Under **Group Commit** (`DeferStrictSyncGuard`), per-op sync barriers are deferred; the batch drainer issues one flush per involved `DiskManager` after applying all ops in memory. | | **LegacyWholeMmapAsync** | 3 | Async | `msync(MS_ASYNC)` | Entire virtual memory map | Legacy behavior; kept for compatibility. | ### RangeAsync Batching - `RANGE_ASYNC_BATCH_OPS = 64` — drain after 64 mutations. - `RANGE_ASYNC_BATCH_BYTES = 4 MiB` — drain after 4 MiB of dirty data. - `RANGE_ASYNC_FALLBACK_INLINE_OPS = 256` — safety cap; forces inline drain if internal callers bypass public wrappers. - `async_drain_ready` (atomic flag) signals the caller to invoke `drain_pending_async_ranges()` (done automatically at the end of public mutating APIs via `maybe_drain_async_ranges()`). - Coalescing expands ranges to page/block boundaries (4 KiB), sorts, merges overlapping/contiguous, and bridges gaps ≤ 1 MiB. ### Strict Mode Group Commit When multiple `Strict` mutations are submitted concurrently via `submit_group_write_op()` ([`src/disk.rs#L9323-L9440`](../../src/disk.rs#L9323-L9440)): 1. A dedicated **group-commit worker thread** (`oifs-group-commit`) collects up to 128 operations into a batch. 2. Enters `DeferStrictSyncGuard` (thread-local flag) which causes `is_strict_sync_deferred()` to return `true`, suppressing per-op `msync(MS_SYNC)` inside `sync_mutation_ranges()`. 3. Executes all operations in memory (under each operation's exclusive write lock). 4. After the batch, **deduplicates** `DiskManager` instances by `Arc` pointer and issues **one `flush()` per unique `DiskManager`**. 5. Notifies each caller's completion callback with the result (or flush error). This amortizes the `msync(MS_SYNC)` syscall across many operations while preserving per-operation durability semantics. ### Kani-Verified Invariants The durability enum has machine-checked proofs ([`src/disk.rs#L9888-L9910`](../../src/disk.rs#L9888-L9910)): - `proof_durability_mode_from_u8_soundness`: lossless round-tripping for all `u8` inputs. - `proof_durability_mode_is_range_based_consistency`: `is_range_based()` is `true` iff `RangeAsync` or `Strict`. ## Write Path: `write_data_with_filters` The write path uses a **three-stage design** to minimize exclusive lock hold time ([`src/disk.rs#L5879-L6107`](../../src/disk.rs#L5879-L6107)): ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller participant Stage1 as Stage 1: Shared Read Lock participant Stage2 as Stage 2: CPU-Bound (No Locks) participant Stage3 as Stage 3: Exclusive Write Lock participant Journal as Journal (if enabled) Caller->>Stage1: write_data_with_filters(inode_id, offset, data, ...) Stage1->>Stage1: Read inode, detect Seekable 64K fast path alt Seekable 64K / Encrypted Partial Upgrade Stage1->>Stage1: prepare_chunked_64k_stage1 Stage1-->>Stage3: Stage1Prep::Seekable (hand off to chunked pipeline) else Standard Path Stage1->>Stage1: Read existing decompressed data if needed Stage1-->>Stage2: Stage1Prep::Standard (inode, gen, existing, key, scheme) end Stage2->>Stage2: plan_write_prepared (filters, compression, encryption) Note right of Stage2: Pure CPU work: delta/shuffle/bitshuffle,
Zstd frame compress, XChaCha20 AEAD encrypt Stage2-->>Stage3: WritePlan (buffer, new size, ranges, encryption nonce, case) Stage3->>Stage3: Acquire exclusive write lock Stage3->>Stage3: Verify inode_gen unchanged (staleness check) alt Staleness check passes Stage3->>Stage3: Use prepared plan else Staleness check fails Stage3->>Stage3: Re-compute plan under write lock (plan_write) end alt Journaled Stage3->>Journal: Stage via AllocSim, commit WAL tx, apply ops else Legacy Stage3->>Stage3: In-place block allocation + write + inode update end Stage3->>Stage3: sync_mutation_ranges per durability mode Stage3-->>Caller: Result ``` ### Stage 1 — Shared Read Lock (`inner.read()`) - Reads the inode and determines the compression/encryption path. - **Seekable 64K fast path**: If `INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K` is set or `CompressionMode::Seekable` is requested, or if a non-zero-offset write on an encrypted Format-v2+ file without filters triggers **encrypted partial upgrade** (transparent upgrade to 64 KiB context-bound AEAD chunks), the method delegates to `finish_chunked_64k_pipeline` and returns early. - Otherwise, captures `initial_inode`, `initial_gen` (from `inode_write_gen`), existing decompressed data (if transformed payload requires read-modify-recompress), encryption key, and encryption scheme. The shared lock is **dropped immediately** after this snapshot. ### Stage 2 — CPU-Bound Processing (Zero Filesystem Locks) - `plan_write_prepared` executes the full filter→compress→encrypt pipeline on the caller's thread: - **Filters**: Delta, Shuffle, Bitshuffle (typesize-aware). - **Compression**: Zstd frame (pooled `CCtx` to avoid per-call allocation). Modes: `Always`, `Never`, `Auto` (≥ 8 KiB), `Stream` (explicit level), `Seekable` (64 KiB independent chunks). - **Encryption**: XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD in-place (nonce generated, AAD bound to `inode_id` and encryption scheme version). - Produces a `WritePlan` enum with four cases: - **FullOverwrite**: Offset 0 rewrite with full filter-compression-encryption pipeline. - **CompressedAppend**: Fast Zstd frame append at EOF for eligible compressed files (unencrypted, no filters, appending at EOF). - **Recompress**: Read-modify-recompress for compressed files when fast path unavailable. - **Raw**: Direct block writes for uncompressed files. ### Stage 3 — Exclusive Lock Acquisition & Commit - Acquires `inner.write()`. - Verifies inode still allocated and `inode_gen(inode_id) == initial_gen` (lock-free staleness detection). - If generation matches, uses the prepared plan; otherwise re-computes under the write lock via `plan_write`. - **Journaled images**: Stages through `AllocSim`, commits a single CRC32C WAL transaction (`commit_journal_tx` + `apply_journal_ops`), updates hints. - **Legacy images**: In-place block allocation, payload write, inode update. - Calls `sync_mutation_ranges` per durability mode; drains `RangeAsync` batch via `maybe_drain_async_ranges`. ### Atomic Rename `DiskManager::rename` ([`src/disk.rs#L7532-L7930`](../../src/disk.rs#L7532-L7930)) provides POSIX atomic rename with crash safety: - **Metadata-only**: Never reads, decrypts, re-compresses, or copies file payload blocks. On encrypted images, only the directory entry's SIV-encrypted filename is recomputed for the new parent (payload AEAD is bound to `inode_id`). - **POSIX overwrite semantics**: Atomic replacement of regular files (target blocks/inode freed), empty directories (removed), mismatch errors (`Is a directory` / `Not a directory`), cycle prevention (moving a directory into itself or descendants rejected). - **Crash safety**: On journaled images, the entire rename (source unlink, optional target overwrite + block/inode release, destination link, parent inode updates) is committed in a **single atomic CRC32C WAL transaction**. - Implementation stages post-images of modified directory blocks in a `BTreeMap`, builds journal ops for block writes, inode updates, and bitmap frees, then commits and applies atomically. ## Asynchronous I/O: `OifsAsyncTask` Inline Fast-Path `OifsAsyncTask` ([`src/disk.rs#L9049-L9210`](../../src/disk.rs#L9049-L9210)) is a lightweight future that implements `std::future::Future` for zero-dependency `.await` in any Rust async runtime, while also supporting synchronous polling (`is_ready`, `try_take`) and blocking wait (`wait`). ### Inline Fast-Path (~50 ns) Hot cache-hit and `Mmap` reads complete **without spawning or waking background threads**: ```text flowchart TD Caller[Caller] --> TryRead[try_read_at_inline_into / try_read_at_inline_vec] TryRead --> Guard[inner.try_read()?] Guard --> CacheHit{Cache Hit?} CacheHit -->|Mmap Raw| MmapCopy[memcpy from mmap slice] CacheHit -->|FileIo DataPageCache| PageCacheCopy[copy from page cache] CacheHit -->|ChunkReadCache| ChunkCopy[decompressed chunk slice] CacheHit -->|DecodedBlobCache| BlobCopy[decoded payload slice] CacheHit -->|Miss| None[Return None] MmapCopy --> Ready[OifsAsyncTask::ready(Ok(n))] PageCacheCopy --> Ready ChunkCopy --> Ready BlobCopy --> Ready None --> Spawn[OifsAsyncTask::spawn(background read)] ``` - `try_read_at_inline_into` probes caches under a non-blocking `try_read()` guard: 1. **Seekable 64K**: Single-chunk `ChunkReadCache` hit. 2. **Compressed/Encrypted/Filtered**: `DecodedBlobCache` hit. 3. **Raw uncompressed/unencrypted**: `Mmap` direct slice or `FileIo` `DataPageCache` hit via `try_read_data_cached_only`. - On hit, returns `Some(Ok(bytes))` immediately; caller wraps in `OifsAsyncTask::ready`. - On miss, returns `None`; caller falls back to `OifsAsyncTask::spawn` which submits to a persistent async read/compute thread pool (2–8 workers, `oifs-async-N`). ### Background Pool - `submit_async_job` enqueues work to a global `AsyncPoolQueue` with a condition variable. - Workers are spawned once on first use; pool size = `available_parallelism().clamp(2, 8)`. - `OifsAsyncTask::wait()` blocks synchronously; `poll()` enables async `.await`. ## Journaling and Recovery The metadata WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) subsystem ([`src/journal.rs`](../../src/journal.rs)) provides crash-safe metadata mutations: - **Geometry**: Journaled images reserve blocks 3–35 for journal (1 header + 32 ring blocks = 132 KiB). Inode table starts at block 36 (vs. block 3 for non-journaled). - **Idempotent redo**: Every `MetadataOp` is a post-image write or absolute bit set (never incremental). Replaying any number of times yields the same state. - **Torn-write detection**: Each frame carries CRC32C (Castagnoli) over header+payload + trailing commit marker (`0xDEAD_BEEF`). Partially written frames fail verification and are discarded. - **Mount-time recovery**: `recover_journal` replays all durable-but-unapplied transactions **before** the `DiskManager` is published. Zero callers observe mid-replay state. - **Clean-shutdown marker**: On clean unmount, a marker is written so next mount can distinguish clean vs. crashed without a ring scan. - **Read-only mount verification**: `is_journal_clean_read_only` checks `pending_txs == 0` with zero disk writes. ## Flush and Drop Semantics - `DiskManager::flush()`: Explicit synchronous flush of all dirty data (journal region first, then backing). - `Drop`: - **Read-write**: Flushes journal region (if journaled) then backing. - **Read-only**: **Zero disk writes** (`should_sync_on_drop` returns `(false, false)`). - `set_durability_mode`: Switching away from `RangeAsync` drains pending async ranges immediately. ## Configuration & Operations ### Durability Mode API ```rust dm.durability_mode() // Get current mode dm.set_durability_mode(Strict) // Set mode (drains RangeAsync if leaving it) dm.with_durability_mode(Strict) // Builder pattern ``` ### Read-Only Detection ```rust dm.is_read_only() // bool ``` ### Storage Mode ```rust dm.storage_mode() // StorageMode::Mmap or FileIo dm.set_file_io_cache_bytes(n) // User-space page cache budget (FileIo only) dm.file_io_cache_bytes() // Configured capacity dm.file_io_cache_used_bytes() // Current usage ``` ## Invariants & Failure Modes | Invariant | Enforcement | |-----------|-------------| | Exclusive access per image | POSIX advisory lock (`F_SETLK`/`F_RDLCK`) held for `DiskManager` lifetime | | No mutation on read-only | `read_only` flag checked at start of every mutating public API; returns `DiskManagerError::ReadOnly` | | Journal replay before publish | `recover_journal` called in `init_or_open_with_key` before returning `DiskManager` | | Read-only rejects dirty journal | `validate_read_only_journal_state` rejects `pending_txs > 0` | | WAL-before-metadata ordering | `flush_async_batch` flushes journal region first; Group Commit deduplicates Strict flushes | | Inode generation staleness detection | `inode_write_gen` per-slot counter; Stage 1 captures `initial_gen`, Stage 3 verifies before commit | | Crash-safe format migration | `migration_cursor` records progress; readers decode per-slot version; `checkpoint_journal` precedes rewrite | | Atomic rename on journaled images | Single WAL transaction commits source unlink, target overwrite, dest link, parent updates | ## Extension Points - **Pluggable I/O backends**: `IoEngine` with `Mmap`, `Pread`, `IoUring` (selected via `OIFS_IO_BACKEND` env var or `StorageMode`). - **Compression modes**: `CompressionMode` enum with `Auto`, `Always`, `Never`, `Stream`, `Seekable`. - **Filters**: `FilterConfig` (delta, shuffle, bitshuffle, typesize) applied pre-compression. - **Encryption**: XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD with Argon2id key derivation; scheme versioning (`ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_CONTEXT_BOUND`). - **Async read pool**: Global `submit_async_job` for CPU-bound decompression/decryption offload. - **Group commit**: `submit_group_write_op` for batched Strict-mode sync amortization. ## Focused Tests - **Kani proofs** (`src/disk.rs` verification module): - `proof_durability_mode_from_u8_soundness` - `proof_durability_mode_is_range_based_consistency` - `proof_get_block_checked_arithmetic_prevents_wrap_around` - `proof_inode_byte_range_checked_bounds` - `proof_write_from_start_size_invariant` - `proof_read_only_mount_drop_and_open_mode_invariants` - `proof_read_only_storage_access_invariants` - **Journal recovery tests**: Corrupt frame detection, torn write simulation, clean vs. crashed mount discrimination. - **Read-only mount tests**: `0444` file open, shared lock concurrency, dirty journal rejection. - **Durability mode tests**: `RangeAsync` batch coalescing, `Strict` group commit deduplication, `Lazy` no-flush behavior. - **Rename tests**: Overwrite semantics, cycle prevention, journaled atomicity, encrypted filename recomputation. - **Write path tests**: Seekable 64K fast path, compressed append, recompress fallback, filter-compress-encrypt pipeline.

nodes.title: Encryption & Filename Obfuscation
nodes.description: Argon2id KDF, BLAKE2b-512 subkeys, XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD for data, 192-bit SIV for filenames, and key management.
nodes.body:
## Responsibility and ownership

The encryption subsystem (`src/encryption.rs`) provides cryptographic privacy and authenticated integrity for stored files, directory entries, and on-disk metadata. It isolates cryptographic primitives into clean layers:

1. **Key Management and Hygiene**: Passphrase hashing with Argon2id, master-key-to-subkey derivation via BLAKE2b domain separation, and automatic secret erasure via `ZeroizeOnDrop` ([`EncryptionKey`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L49-L111)).
2. **File Payload AEAD**: Authenticated payload confidentiality via [`encrypt_data`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L184-L213) / [`decrypt_data`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L215-L241) and in-place variants.
3. **Seekable Chunk AEAD**: Context-bound encryption for 64 KiB seekable chunks with AAD binding `inode_id`, `chunk_idx`, and `flags` ([`chunk_aad_stack`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L358-L375)).
4. **Deterministic Filename Privacy**: SIV construction using BLAKE2b-512 synthetic nonce + XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, parent inode bound in AAD ([`encrypt_filename`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L661-L779), [`decrypt_filename`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L770-L901)).
5. **IPC Authentication**: Dedicated subkey for challenge-response authentication (`ipc_auth_key`).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    %% Key derivation hierarchy
    MasterKey["Master Key (256-bit)\nArgon2id(m=64MiB, t=3, p=4)\nor externally supplied"]
    derive["derive_subkey(master, context)\nBLAKE2b-512\n'OIFS-BLAKE2B-SUBKEY-KDF-V2' || len(context) || context || master"]
    PayloadKey["payload_key\nKDF_CONTEXT_PAYLOAD\n'oifs.kdf.v2.payload.xchacha20poly1305'\n→ XChaCha20-Poly1305 file & chunk payloads"]
    FilenameSIVKey["filename_siv_key\nKDF_CONTEXT_FILENAME_SIV\n'oifs.kdf.v2.filename.siv.blake2b'\n→ BLAKE2b-512 synthetic nonce for SIV"]
    FilenameCipherKey["filename_cipher_key\nKDF_CONTEXT_FILENAME_CIPHER\n'oifs.kdf.v2.filename.aead.xchacha20poly1305'\n→ XChaCha20-Poly1305 filename AEAD"]
    IPCAuthKey["ipc_auth_key\nKDF_CONTEXT_IPC_AUTH\n'oifs.kdf.v2.ipc.auth.blake2b'\n→ BLAKE2b IPC challenge-response"]

    MasterKey --> derive
    derive --> PayloadKey
    derive --> FilenameSIVKey
    derive --> FilenameCipherKey
    derive --> IPCAuthKey
```

**Figure**: Encryption key hierarchy — a single 256-bit master key produces four domain-separated 256-bit subkeys via BLAKE2b-512. The master key is never used directly for any cryptographic operation.

## Key derivation and memory hygiene

### Memory hygiene with ZeroizeOnDrop

[`EncryptionKey`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L49-L111) wraps the master key and all four subkeys with `zeroize` macros:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]
pub struct EncryptionKey {
    /// Master 256-bit key derived from Argon2id (or supplied directly)
    key: [u8; 32],
    /// Domain-separated 256-bit subkey for file and seekable-chunk XChaCha20-Poly1305 payloads
    payload_key: [u8; 32],
    /// Domain-separated 256-bit subkey for filename SIV BLAKE2b-512 synthetic nonce derivation
    filename_siv_key: [u8; 32],
    /// Domain-separated 256-bit subkey for filename XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD encryption
    filename_cipher_key: [u8; 32],
    /// Domain-separated 256-bit subkey for IPC challenge-response authentication
    ipc_auth_key: [u8; 32],
}
```

- When an `EncryptionKey` instance goes out of scope, `ZeroizeOnDrop` automatically executes volatile memory zeroization on all five `[u8; 32]` arrays.
- The `fmt::Debug` implementation explicitly overrides formatted output with `EncryptionKey([REDACTED])` ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L109-L111](repo://src/encryption.rs#L109-L111)), preventing secrets from accidentally leaking into log outputs or panic strings.
- `derive_subkey` also zeroizes the intermediate BLAKE2b-512 digest after extracting the 32-byte subkey ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L24-L44](repo://src/encryption.rs#L24-L44)).

### Argon2id password-based key derivation (PBKDF)

Keys are derived from user-supplied passphrases using Argon2id via [`derive_key`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L124-L167):

- **Parameters**: `m = 65,536 KiB (64 MiB)`, `t = 3`, `p = 4` (OWASP / RFC 9106 hardened defaults). Constants are [`ARGON2_M_COST_KIB`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L7-L9), [`ARGON2_T_COST`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L7-L9), [`ARGON2_P_COST`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L7-L9).
- **Salt Management**: A cryptographically secure 16-byte random salt is generated with `OsRng` via [`generate_salt()`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L301-L306). This salt is permanently stored in plaintext within the filesystem's `SuperBlock::encryption_salt` ([repo://src/superblock.rs#L47](repo://src/superblock.rs#L47)).
- **Rainbow Table and GPU Resistance**: Argon2id combines data-dependent and data-independent memory access passes, providing state-of-the-art resistance against both side-channel cache timing attacks and GPU/ASIC password cracking.
- The 256-bit output hash is copied into `EncryptionKey::from_bytes(key)`, which immediately derives the four domain-separated subkeys via BLAKE2b-512.
- The master key buffer is zeroized immediately after subkey derivation ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L161-L163](repo://src/encryption.rs#L161-L163)).

### BLAKE2b-512 domain-separated subkey derivation

The [`derive_subkey`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L24-L44) function ensures the master key is never reused directly across distinct primitives:

```rust
pub fn derive_subkey(master_key: &[u8; 32], context: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
    let mut hasher = Blake2b512::new();
    hasher.update(b"OIFS-BLAKE2B-SUBKEY-KDF-V2");
    hasher.update([context.len() as u8]);
    hasher.update(context);
    hasher.update(master_key);
    let digest = hasher.finalize();
    let mut subkey = [0u8; 32];
    subkey.copy_from_slice(&digest[..32]);
    digest.zeroize();
    subkey
}
```

Domain separation labels (constants at [repo://src/encryption.rs#L13-L16](repo://src/encryption.rs#L13-L16)):
- `KDF_CONTEXT_PAYLOAD` = `b"oifs.kdf.v2.payload.xchacha20poly1305"`
- `KDF_CONTEXT_FILENAME_SIV` = `b"oifs.kdf.v2.filename.siv.blake2b"`
- `KDF_CONTEXT_FILENAME_CIPHER` = `b"oifs.kdf.v2.filename.aead.xchacha20poly1305"`
- `KDF_CONTEXT_IPC_AUTH` = `b"oifs.kdf.v2.ipc.auth.blake2b"`

Each label is distinct and versioned (`v2`), guaranteeing cryptographic isolation: `payload_key` ≠ `filename_siv_key` ≠ `filename_cipher_key` ≠ `ipc_auth_key` ≠ `master_key`. Tests verify pairwise distinctness ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L1000-L1013](repo://src/encryption.rs#L1000-L1013)).

## Encryption schemes (versioning)

The filesystem records `encryption_version` in the superblock ([repo://src/superblock.rs#L47](repo://src/superblock.rs#L47)). Two schemes exist:

| Scheme | Constant | Value | AAD |
|--------|----------|-------|-----|
| Legacy | `ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_LEGACY` | 1 | Empty (no binding) |
| Context-bound | `ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_CONTEXT_BOUND` | 2 | Binds `inode_id` / `chunk_idx` / `flags` / `parent_inode` |

- New images always use `ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_CONTEXT_BOUND` ([repo://src/disk.rs#L1659](repo://src/disk.rs#L1659), [repo://src/disk.rs#L1669](repo://src/disk.rs#L1669)).
- Legacy images (scheme 1) remain readable; their AAD is empty, so ciphertexts can be moved across files/chunks without authentication failure.
- `file_aad_for_scheme_stack` / `chunk_aad_for_scheme_stack` ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L387-L423](repo://src/encryption.rs#L387-L423)) select the appropriate AAD based on the scheme version.
- Validation rejects unencrypted images with non-zero version, and encrypted images with unknown version ([repo://src/superblock.rs#L462-L467](repo://src/superblock.rs#L462-L467)).

## Context-bound Associated Data (AAD)

AAD construction is stack-allocated (zero heap allocations) and domain-separated by a leading kind byte.

| Kind | Constant | Layout (bytes) | Binds |
|------|----------|----------------|-------|
| File | `AAD_KIND_FILE` (0x01) | `[kind][AAD_DOMAIN(11)][inode_id(8)]` = 20 | `inode_id` |
| Chunk | `AAD_KIND_CHUNK` (0x02) | `[kind][AAD_DOMAIN(11)][inode_id(8)][chunk_idx(8)][flags(1)]` = 29 | `inode_id`, `chunk_idx`, `flags` |
| Filename | `AAD_KIND_FILENAME` (0x03) | `[kind][AAD_DOMAIN(11)][parent_inode(8)]` = 20 | `parent_inode` |

- `AAD_DOMAIN = b"OIFS-AAD-v1"` (11 bytes).
- Functions: `file_aad_stack`, `chunk_aad_stack`, `filename_aad_stack` ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L348-L375](repo://src/encryption.rs#L348-L375)).
- Kani proof verifies domain separation and injectivity ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L1138-L1164](repo://src/encryption.rs#L1138-L1164)).

## XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD encryption/decryption

### File/chunk payloads

- **Nonce**: 192-bit (24 bytes) generated via `generate_nonce()` ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L308-L312](repo://src/encryption.rs#L308-L312)) — cryptographically random, unique per encryption.
- **Key**: `payload_key` (256-bit subkey).
- **AAD**: `file_aad_stack(inode_id)` for whole files, `chunk_aad_stack(inode_id, chunk_idx, flags)` for seekable chunks.
- **Operations**: `encrypt_data`, `decrypt_data`, `encrypt_data_in_place`, `decrypt_data_in_place`, `encrypt_with_nonce_prefix`, `decrypt_into_slice` ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L184-L297](repo://src/encryption.rs#L184-L297)).
- **Ciphertext layout**: `[24-byte nonce | ciphertext | 16-byte Poly1305 tag]` (produced by `encrypt_with_nonce_prefix`).

### Short-message scalar fast path

On `aarch64` with NEON, the library's `chacha20` crate computes 4 blocks (256 B) per call and discards 3 for short messages — wasting 75% of work on filenames (`≤ 64 B`). A scalar RFC 8439 + XChaCha20 implementation (`xchacha20_poly1305_encrypt_short` / `xchacha20_poly1305_decrypt_short`, [repo://src/encryption.rs#L446-L560](repo://src/encryption.rs#L446-L560)) computes only the exact 64-byte blocks needed, remaining **byte-for-byte identical** to the reference implementation (proven by exhaustive test up to 192 bytes [repo://src/encryption.rs#L1070-L1115](repo://src/encryption.rs#L1070-L1115)). Threshold: `SHORT_XCHACHA_THRESHOLD = 192` bytes ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L331](repo://src/encryption.rs#L331)).

- Uses `hchacha20` to derive a 256-bit subkey from the 192-bit nonce's first 16 bytes.
- Generates Poly1305 key from ChaCha20 block 0; encrypts with blocks 1..N.
- All intermediate key material (subkey, Poly1305 key, per-block keystream) is zeroized after use ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L525-L555](repo://src/encryption.rs#L525-L555)).
- Used automatically by `encrypt_filename` and `decrypt_filename_authenticated` for payloads ≤ 192 bytes.

## Filename encryption: 192-bit SIV (deterministic, collision-resistant)

### Construction

1. **Synthetic nonce (SIV)**: 24-byte (192-bit) derived via BLAKE2b-512 keyed by `filename_siv_key`:
   ```
   nonce = BLAKE2b-512("OIFS_SIV_FILENAME_V2_XCHACHA20" || filename_siv_key || parent_inode(8) || name)[0..24]
   ```
   ([`derive_filename_siv_nonce`](repo://src/encryption.rs#L629-L639))

2. **AEAD encryption**: XChaCha20-Poly1305 with `filename_cipher_key`, the 24-byte nonce, and `filename_aad_stack(parent_inode)` as AAD.

3. **Output format**: ASCII string `_e_` + Base64URL-unpadded(`nonce(24) || ciphertext || tag(16)`). Prefix `_e_` marks encrypted entries ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L323](repo://src/encryption.rs#L323)).

### Security properties

- **Deterministic**: Same `(key, parent_inode, name)` → identical ciphertext. Enables directory listing without decryption.
- **Tweakable**: Different `parent_inode` → different ciphertext for same name. Prevents cross-directory correlation.
- **Authentication**: Poly1305 tag covers ciphertext + AAD (parent inode). Tampering detected.
- **SIV verification**: On decryption, the derived nonce is recomputed from candidate plaintext and compared in constant time (`ct_eq_slice`). Rejects ciphertexts where nonce was forged ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L815-L825](repo://src/encryption.rs#L815-L825)).
- **Legacy fallback**: Reads v1 12-byte `ChaCha20Poly1305` format (`OIFS_SIV_FILENAME_V1`) for backward compatibility when `encryption_version < ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_CONTEXT_BOUND` ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L735-L779](repo://src/encryption.rs#L735-L779)). Anti-downgrade: v1 tokens rejected on v2+ images.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as User (password)
    participant KDF as Argon2id KDF
    participant Master as Master Key (32 B)
    participant Subkeys as BLAKE2b Subkey Derivation
    participant Payload as XChaCha20-Poly1305 (payload_key)
    participant Filename as SIV + XChaCha20-Poly1305 (filename_*_keys)
    participant IPC as BLAKE2b-MAC (ipc_auth_key)

    User->>KDF: password + salt (16 B)
    KDF->>Master: 256-bit hash (m=64MiB, t=3, p=4)
    Master->>Subkeys: "OIFS-BLAKE2B-SUBKEY-KDF-V2" || len(ctx) || ctx || master
    Subkeys->>Payload: payload_key
    Subkeys->>Filename: filename_siv_key, filename_cipher_key
    Subkeys->>IPC: ipc_auth_key

    Note over Payload: File payload encryption
    Payload->>Payload: nonce ← OsRng(24 B)
    Payload->>Payload: AAD ← file_aad_stack(inode_id) / chunk_aad_stack(inode_id, chunk_idx, flags)
    Payload->>Payload: ciphertext || tag ← XChaCha20-Poly1305(payload_key, nonce, AAD, plaintext)

    Note over Filename: Filename encryption (deterministic)
    Filename->>Filename: nonce ← BLAKE2b-512("OIFS_SIV_FILENAME_V2_XCHACHA20" || filename_siv_key || parent_inode || name)[0..24]
    Filename->>Filename: AAD ← filename_aad_stack(parent_inode)
    Filename->>Filename: ciphertext || tag ← XChaCha20-Poly1305(filename_cipher_key, nonce, AAD, name)
    Filename->>Filename: output ← "_e_" || Base64URL(nonce || ciphertext || tag)

    Note over IPC: IPC challenge-response
    IPC->>IPC: client_nonce (32 B), server_nonce (32 B), salt (16 B)
    IPC->>IPC: transcript ← direction(1) || client_nonce || server_nonce || salt
    IPC->>IPC: mac ← BLAKE2b-MAC(ipc_auth_key, transcript, domain="OIFS-IPC-AUTH-V1")
```

## Seekable 64 KiB chunk encryption

### Write path

In `DiskManager::prepare_chunk_payload` ([repo://src/disk/chunked.rs#L288-L330](repo://src/disk/chunked.rs#L288-L330)):
1. If compression yields smaller output, use compressed data; otherwise use raw 64 KiB chunk.
2. Generate fresh 24-byte nonce via `generate_nonce()`.
3. Build AAD via `chunk_aad_for_scheme_stack(inode_id, chunk_idx, flags, scheme)` where `flags` is `FLAG_COMPRESSED` (1) or `FLAG_RAW` (2).
4. Encrypt with `encrypt_with_nonce_prefix` → `[nonce | ciphertext | tag]`.
5. Store payload in the chunk's block run; record `compressed_len` and `block_count` in `ChunkEntry`.

### Read path

In `DiskManager::read_single_chunk_into` ([repo://src/disk/chunked.rs#L420-L490](repo://src/disk/chunked.rs#L420-L490)):
1. Read ciphertext from block run (handles both mmap and pread).
2. Extract 24-byte nonce, ciphertext+tag.
3. Rebuild identical AAD via `chunk_aad_for_scheme_stack(inode_id, chunk_idx, flags, scheme)`.
4. Decrypt with `decrypt_into_slice` directly into caller's destination buffer (zero intermediate copy for the happy path).
5. If compressed, decompress with Zstd into destination.

### Security properties

- **Per-chunk unique nonce**: Fresh 24-byte random nonce per encryption.
- **AAD binding**: `inode_id`, `chunk_idx`, and `flags` prevent chunk reordering, rollback, or cross-file injection.
- **Flag authentication**: Compressed vs. raw flag is authenticated; an attacker cannot flip the flag to bypass decompression or cause type confusion.
- **Encrypted inode requirement**: On encrypted filesystems, seekable files must have `inode.encrypted = true`; otherwise reads fail with `DecryptionFailed` ([repo://src/disk/chunked.rs#L384-L387](repo://src/disk/chunked.rs#L384-L387)).

## IPC challenge-response authentication

### Protocol

1. **Client → Server**: `AuthChallenge { client_nonce[32], has_password }`
2. **Server → Client**: `AuthChallenge { server_nonce[32], salt[16], encrypted }`
3. **Client → Server**: `AuthResponse { client_mac[32] }`
4. **Server → Client**: `AuthVerify { server_mac[32] }` (mutual authentication)

### Transcript construction

```rust
transcript = direction(1) || client_nonce(32) || server_nonce(32) || salt(16)
```
- `direction = 0` for client→server, `1` for server→client (prevents tag reflection).
- MAC = `BLAKE2b-MAC(ipc_auth_key, transcript, personal="OIFS-IPC-AUTH-V1")` ([repo://src/ipc.rs#L318-L331](repo://src/ipc.rs#L318-L331)).

### Key source

- **Encrypted images**: Client derives `ipc_auth_key` from password + salt (same Argon2id+BLAKE2b derivation as master). Password never travels on the wire.
- **Unencrypted images**: Master generates a 32-byte session secret via `generate_auth_secret()`, publishes hex-encoded in `.image.master` rendezvous file (`auth_token` field); client reads and uses directly ([repo://src/ipc.rs#L886-L982](repo://src/ipc.rs#L886-L982)).

### Security properties

- **10-second handshake timeout** (`AUTH_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`) prevents Slowloris attacks ([repo://src/ipc.rs#L161](repo://src/ipc.rs#L161)).
- **Authenticated streams are pooled** to avoid repeated handshakes ([repo://src/ipc.rs#L1407-L1412](repo://src/ipc.rs#L1407-L1412)).
- **Constant-time tag comparison** (`ct_eq`) prevents timing side channels ([repo://src/ipc.rs#L333-L340](repo://src/ipc.rs#L333-L340)).
- Password verifier stored in `DiskManagerInner` uses BLAKE2b-512 with domain `OIFS-PWD-VERIFIER-V1` over `ipc_auth_key || password` ([repo://src/disk.rs#L1541-L1553](repo://src/disk.rs#L1541-L1553)).

## Per-file key hierarchy and key rotation considerations

### Current design

- **Single master key per filesystem**: All files, chunks, and filenames derive from the same `EncryptionKey` hierarchy (master + 4 subkeys).
- **Per-object nonces**: Files and chunks use fresh random 192-bit nonces per encryption. Filenames use deterministic SIV nonces derived from `(parent_inode, name)`.
- **AAD binding**: Context-bound scheme binds ciphertexts to their logical location (`inode_id`, `chunk_idx`, `flags`, `parent_inode`), preventing cut-and-paste and rollback attacks.

### Key rotation implications

| Operation | Current support | Notes |
|-----------|----------------|-------|
| Password change | Requires full re-encryption | Master key changes → all subkeys change → all ciphertexts must be rewritten. |
| Subkey rotation | Not supported | No mechanism to rotate individual subkeys without changing master key. |
| Scheme upgrade | Supported (legacy → context-bound) | New files use v2; existing v1 files readable but not automatically upgraded. |
| Master key rotation | Not supported | Would require re-encrypting entire filesystem (all files, chunks, filenames, inodes). |

**Design note**: The filesystem stores `encryption_salt` (16 B) and `encryption_version` (1 B) in the superblock. A key rotation feature would need:
1. A new salt + Argon2id derivation → new master key.
2. Re-encryption of every payload, chunk, and filename.
3. Atomic superblock update with new salt/version.
4. Crash-safe journaling of the re-encryption operation (supported via existing WAL).

## Data structures summary

### `EncryptionConfig` (scheme selection)

```rust
pub const ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_LEGACY: u8 = 1;           // Empty AAD
pub const ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_CONTEXT_BOUND: u8 = 2;    // Binds inode/chunk/filename context
```

Stored in `SuperBlock.encryption_version` ([repo://src/superblock.rs#L47](repo://src/superblock.rs#L47)).

### `MasterKey` (opaque 256-bit)

- Directly output of Argon2id or externally supplied.
- Never used for encryption directly.

### `FileKey` ≡ `EncryptionKey`

```rust
pub struct EncryptionKey {
    key: [u8; 32],                 // Master
    payload_key: [u8; 32],         // File/chunk XChaCha20-Poly1305
    filename_siv_key: [u8; 32],    // Filename SIV BLAKE2b-512
    filename_cipher_key: [u8; 32], // Filename XChaCha20-Poly1305
    ipc_auth_key: [u8; 32],        // IPC BLAKE2b-MAC
}
```

All five arrays zeroized on drop.

### `SubKey` (domain-separated 256-bit)

Produced by `derive_subkey(master, context)`. Four contexts defined as constants ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L13-L16](repo://src/encryption.rs#L13-L16)).

## Implementation files

| File | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| `src/encryption.rs` | Core primitives: KDF, subkeys, AEAD, SIV filename, short-scalar XChaCha20, AAD builders |
| `src/disk.rs` | Integration: `build_full_overwrite_buffer_pure`, `plan_write_prepared`, `encryption_key` field in `DiskManagerInner`, read/write paths |
| `src/superblock.rs` | `encryption_salt`, `encryption_version`, `encrypted` flag persistence |
| `src/ipc.rs` | Challenge-response handshake using `ipc_auth_key` |
| `src/disk/chunked.rs` | Seekable 64 KiB chunk encryption with `chunk_aad_stack` |

## Tests and verification

- **Unit tests** ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L916-L1115](repo://src/encryption.rs#L916-L1115)):
  - Key derivation determinism and salt isolation
  - Encrypt/decrypt round-trips (payload, in-place, with nonce prefix)
  - Wrong key / wrong nonce rejection
  - Filename encryption determinism, tweakability, legacy fallback, tamper detection
  - Subkey domain separation pairwise distinctness
  - Short-scalar XChaCha20 byte-for-byte equivalence to reference (exhaustive up to 192 B)
  - Argon2id parameter constants match OWASP/RFC 9106

- **Kani formal verification** ([repo://src/encryption.rs#L1138-L1164](repo://src/encryption.rs#L1138-L1164)):
  - AAD kind tags never collide across file/chunk/filename domains
  - Filename AAD injective in `parent_inode`
  - `file_aad_stack`, `chunk_aad_stack`, `filename_aad_stack` encode IDs bijectively

## Related pages

- [Compression and Filters](../architecture/compression_and_filters.md) — Filter → Compress → Encrypt pipeline
- [Disk Manager and Persistence](../architecture/disk_manager_and_persistence.md) — Write paths, journaling, durability modes
- [Encrypted Workflows](../workflows/encrypted_workflows.md) — End-to-end encrypted filesystem operations

nodes.body:
# Files

- [Async I/O Engine and Group Commit](async_io_and_engines.md) - Covers the pluggable I/O backend system (Mmap, Pread, IoUring), ExtentList coalescing, io_uring capability gating, async read engine with inline fast-path, and async write engine with group commit for DurabilityMode::Strict.
- [Block & Inode Allocation](block_allocation.md) - Documents the bitmap-based block allocator (SimpleBlockAllocator), inode allocator, free space tracking, allocation strategies (hints, contiguous runs), multi-block bitmap layout (v3), hardware-accelerated tzcnt scanning, BitmapSliceMut write-through mirrors for FileIo mode, and allocation simulation for WAL transactions.
- [Compression & Pre-Compression Filters](compression_and_filters.md) - Seekable 64 KiB chunked compression (Zstd), SIMD pre-filters (Delta, Shuffle, BitShuffle, TruncPrecision), ZstdContextPool with persistent scoped worker pool, DecodedBlobCache and ChunkReadCache for read acceleration, and cache invalidation across write/truncate/defrag.
- [Concurrency and session](concurrency_and_session.md)
- [Online Defragmentation and Auto-Defrag](defragmentation.md) - How OIFS analyzes filesystem fragmentation using 64-bit bitmap scanning and performs both safe (out-of-place rebuild with atomic rename) and WAL-atomic in-place defragmentation, including ChunkEntry relocation for seekable files, shift_table_collapse for chunk table compaction, and a background auto-defrag coordinator.
- [DiskManager & Persistence](disk_manager_and_persistence.md) - Central coordinator for OIFS storage: image open/create, superblock management, inode CRUD, data read/write with compression/encryption, durability modes, flush/msync, read-only mounts, and atomic rename.
- [Encryption & Filename Obfuscation](encryption.md) - Argon2id KDF, BLAKE2b-512 subkeys, XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD for data, 192-bit SIV for filenames, and key management.
- [C FFI and C++17/20 API Surface](ffi_interface.md) - Documents the public C FFI (oifs.h) and modern C++ header-only API (oifs.hpp): opaque handles, error codes, sync/async operations, PinnableSlice zero-copy views, and co_await integration.
- [FUSE Kernel Protocol Engine](fuse_engine.md) - Pure-Rust FUSE ABI v7.28 implementation with frame parser/dispatcher, cross-platform mount runners (Linux /dev/fuse + fusermount3, macOS FUSE-T/macFUSE via SCM_RIGHTS), dynamic max_write negotiation, handle table, read-only enforcement, UTF-8 NFD->NFC normalization, and macOS Finder metadata storm protection.
- [Inode Layout and Multi-Block Directories](inode_and_directory.md) - Detailed specification of OIFS's 256-byte inode structure (format v2), directory entry format with filename encryption, block pointer hierarchy, multi-block directory structure with SipHash-2-4 indexing, and directory entry encoding.
- [Filesystem Integrity Checking (fsck)](integrity_checking_fsck.md) - How the OIFS fsck structural consistency scanner performs set-theoretic verification between bitmap allocation states and directory reachability to detect orphan inodes, leaked blocks, missing blocks, and cross-linked blocks, plus read-only journal cleanliness verification. Covers chunk reference validation, deduplication detection, repair strategies, and verification flow.
- [Metadata WAL / Journaling](journal.md) - Describes the transactional metadata write-ahead log (WAL) that ensures crash resilience, including its circular buffer design, CRC32C protection, idempotent redo replay, JBD2-style deferred checkpointing under Strict durability, and DurabilityMode semantics.
- [MCP Server (oifs_mcp)](mcp_server.md) - How the oifs_mcp binary exposes the OIFS storage engine as Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools over stdio, providing AI agents with an isolated, single-file virtual filesystem for persistent memory.
- [Architecture Overview](overview.md) - High-level system map showing owned subsystems, runtime domains, and cross-system data flows for OIFS.
- [Atomic Rename and Metadata Operations](rename_and_atomic_ops.md) - Documents the atomic POSIX rename implementation with WAL transactions, SIV re-encryption for cross-directory moves on encrypted filesystems, FUSE_RENAME/RENAME2 opcode handling, and the MetadataOp journal framing for create/delete/mkdir/rename.
- [Storage Engines](storage_engines.md) - OIFS dual storage backends—Mmap for zero-copy memory-mapped I/O and FileIo for pure positional pread/pwrite I/O—operating over the exact same on-disk format.
- [Superblock and On-Disk Layout](superblock_and_layout.md) - Comprehensive documentation of the OIFS superblock structure, format versioning (v1/v2/v3), block layout geometry, journal region placement, encryption fields, and migration cursor mechanics for in-place format upgrades.

## Responsibility and ownership

The inode and directory subsystem defines the structural foundation of the OIFS filesystem across these modules:

## The 256-byte Inode structure (format v2)

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/inode.rs#L33-L69] file "../src/inode.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
Every file and directory in OIFS is represented by an [`Inode`](../src/inode.rs#L33-L69) stored within the contiguous Inode Table starting at `superblock.inode_table_block`. The on-disk format is **format v2**: a deterministic 256-byte record (`INODE_SLOT_SIZE = 256`) with frozen field offsets `[0..166)`, a `record_version` byte at offset 166, `flags` (u32) at offset 167, and zero padding to byte 256. The in-memory `#[repr(C)]` struct mirrors this layout.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Inode {
    /// Type of this inode (File or Directory)
    pub mode: FileType,
    /// Logical size in bytes (original/uncompressed size)
    pub size: u64,
    /// Physical size in bytes if compressed, 0 if stored raw
    pub compressed_size: u64,
    /// Creation timestamp (Unix epoch seconds)
    pub created_at: u64,
    /// Last modification timestamp (Unix epoch seconds)
    pub modified_at: u64,
    /// Direct block pointers (12 blocks × 4KB = 48KB max file size)
    /// Block ID 0 indicates unallocated/empty block
    pub blocks: [u64; 12],

    // Encryption fields
    /// Is this file encrypted?
    pub encrypted: bool,
    /// Nonce for XChaCha20-Poly1305 (24 bytes, unique per file)
    pub encryption_nonce: [u8; 24],

    // Pre-compression filter fields (blosc2-style pipeline)
    /// Element size for shuffle/delta filters (1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes). 0 = no filters.
    pub filter_typesize: u8,
    /// Whether delta encoding was applied before compression
    pub filter_delta: bool,
    /// Whether byte shuffle was applied before compression
    pub filter_shuffle: bool,
    /// Whether bit shuffle was applied before compression
    pub filter_bitshuffle: bool,

    /// Triple indirect block pointer for files > 1GB (supports up to 513GB)
    pub triple_indirect: u64,

    /// Extended inode flags (e.g. INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K)
    pub flags: u32,
}
```

### On-disk format v2 record layout (fixed 256 bytes)

| Offset | Size | Field | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|-------|
| 0      | 1    | `mode` | `FileType` discriminant (0 = File, 1 = Directory) |
| 1      | 8    | `size` | LE u64 |
| 9      | 8    | `compressed_size` | LE u64 |
| 17     | 8    | `created_at` | LE u64 |
| 25     | 8    | `modified_at` | LE u64 |
| 33     | 96   | `blocks` | 12 × LE u64 |
| 129    | 1    | `encrypted` | bool (0/1) |
| 130    | 24   | `encryption_nonce` | 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce |
| 154    | 1    | `filter_typesize` | u8 (0, 1, 2, 4, 8) |
| 155    | 1    | `filter_delta` | bool |
| 156    | 1    | `filter_shuffle` | bool |
| 157    | 1    | `filter_bitshuffle` | bool |
| 158    | 8    | `triple_indirect` | LE u64 |
| 166    | 1    | `record_version` | Fixed to `2` (format v2) |
| 167    | 4    | `flags` | LE u32 (e.g., `INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K = 0x01`) |
| 171    | 85   | `padding` | Zero-filled to 256 bytes |

The frozen region `[0..166)` is cryptographically bound: any change to those 166 bytes alters the inode's on-disk representation and must be accompanied by a new `record_version` if the layout ever changes. Format v1 (`bincode`-serialized, variable-length) is still decodable via `Inode::decode_v1` but is no longer written.

### FileType discrimination

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum FileType {
    File = 0,
    Directory = 1,
}
```

Only `File` and `Directory` exist. There are no symlinks, device nodes, or other special types in OIFS. The `mode` field is a single byte (offset 0) in the on-disk record.

### Block pointer hierarchy

OIFS uses a three-tier block pointer scheme to support files from a few bytes up to 513 GB:

- **Direct (12)**: `blocks[0..12]` → 12 × 4 KiB = 48 KiB
- **Double indirect**: `triple_indirect` points to a block containing 1024 block IDs (each 8 bytes), each of which points to a data block → 1024 × 1024 × 4 KiB = 4 GiB per double-indirect level
- **Triple indirect**: The `triple_indirect` field points to a level-3 index block. A level-3 block points to 1024 level-2 blocks, each pointing to 1024 data blocks → 1024³ × 4 KiB = 4 TiB theoretical, capped by `u64` logical size and practical limits to ~513 GB.

Block ID `0` always means unallocated/empty. All block IDs are LE u64 on disk.

### Inode encoding/decoding (format v2)

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/inode_format.rs] file "../src/inode_format.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
[`src/inode_format.rs`](../src/inode_format.rs) provides:

- `encode_v2(inode: &Inode) -> [u8; 256]` — deterministic LE encoding matching the table above.
- `decode_v2(bytes: &[u8; 256]) -> Result<Inode, InodeFormatError>` — strict decoding; validates `record_version == 2`, `mode` is valid, and padding bytes 171–255 are zero.
- `decode_v1(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Inode, InodeFormatError>` — legacy `bincode` deserialization for backward compatibility.
- `encode_v1` is not exposed; v1 is read-only.

## Directory entry format and encoding

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/directory.rs#L5-L10] file "../src/directory.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
A directory is a sequence of variable-length [`DirectoryEntry`](../src/directory.rs#L5-L10) records packed contiguously within one or more 4 KiB blocks. There is no on-disk B-tree, hash table, or separate index; lookup is linear scan with SipHash-2-4 filtering.

### On-disk record layout

| Offset | Size | Field | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|-------|
| 0      | 8    | `inode` | LE u64, target inode ID |
| 8      | 8    | `hash` | LE u64, SipHash-2-4 of plaintext filename (or 0 if unhashed) |
| 16     | 2    | `name_len` | LE u16, length of UTF-8 name in bytes (1–255) |
| 18     | `name_len` | `name` | Variable-length UTF-8 filename (no NUL terminator) |

Total per entry = 18 + `name_len` bytes. Max filename length is 255 bytes (`DirectoryEntry::MAX_FILENAME_LEN`). A `name_len` of 0 signals end of entries in the block (remaining bytes are zero-padded).

### Filename encryption in directory entries

When the filesystem is encrypted (`DiskManager::encryption_key` is `Some`), directory entry `name` fields store **ciphertext**, not plaintext. The encryption scheme:

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/encryption.rs#L629-L672] file "../src/encryption.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
1. **Deterministic SIV nonce derivation** (`derive_filename_siv_nonce` in [`src/encryption.rs`](../src/encryption.rs#L629-L672)):
   - Uses BLAKE2b-512 with domain separator `OIFS_SIV_FILENAME_V2_XCHACHA20`
   - Inputs: domain-separated `filename_siv_key` (256-bit), `parent_inode` (u64 LE), plaintext filename bytes
   - Output: 192-bit (24-byte) synthetic IV (`XNonce`)

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/encryption.rs#L647-L720] file "../src/encryption.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
2. **AEAD encryption** (`encrypt_filename` in [`src/encryption.rs`](../src/encryption.rs#L647-L720)):
   - Cipher: XChaCha20-Poly1305 with domain-separated `filename_cipher_key` (256-bit)
   - AAD: `filename_aad_stack(parent_inode)` — 20-byte stack-allocated buffer binding ciphertext to parent directory inode (kind = `AAD_KIND_FILENAME = 0x03`, domain = `OIFS-AAD-v1`, 8-byte parent inode LE)
   - Plaintext: raw UTF-8 filename bytes
   - Output format: `[24-byte XNonce || ciphertext || 16-byte Poly1305 tag]`, then unpadded Base64URL-encoded, prefixed with `_e_`

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/encryption.rs#L752-L855] file "../src/encryption.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
3. **Decryption & verification** (`decrypt_filename_authenticated` in [`src/encryption.rs`](../src/encryption.rs#L752-L855)):
   - Strips `_e_` prefix, Base64URL-decodes
   - Splits payload into 24-byte nonce, ciphertext, 16-byte tag
   - Verifies Poly1305 tag with AAD = `filename_aad_stack(parent_inode)`
   - Decrypts plaintext
   - **Constant-time SIV nonce verification**: recomputes expected nonce via `derive_filename_siv_nonce` and compares with `ct_eq_slice` — prevents nonce-reuse/malleability attacks
   - On failure, falls back to **legacy v1 format** (12-byte `ChaCha20Poly1305` nonce, domain `OIFS_SIV_FILENAME_V1`, no AAD) if `encryption_version < ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_CONTEXT_BOUND` (anti-downgrade)

4. **Plaintext passthrough**: Names not starting with `_e_` pass through `decrypt_filename` unchanged (used for unencrypted filesystems and special entries `.`, `..`).

The `_e_` prefix is a constant (`FILENAME_ENC_PREFIX = "_e_"`) and is itself encrypted if a filename literally begins with `_e_` (deterministic encryption means the same plaintext always produces the same ciphertext).

### SipHash-2-4 directory indexing

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/directory.rs] file "../src/directory.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
[`src/directory.rs`](../src/directory.rs) provides `hash_filename` / `hash_filename_bytes` using SipHash-2-4 with fixed keys (`k0 = 0x0706050403020100`, `k1 = 0x0f0e0d0c0b0a0908`). This 64-bit hash is stored in each `DirectoryEntry.hash` field and used for fast filtering during linear scan (`find_entry_in_block_with_hash`): entries with mismatching hash are skipped without string comparison. Hash value `0` is treated as "no hash" and forces string comparison (backward compatibility).

### Zero-allocation directory operations

All directory block operations work directly on `&[u8]` / `&mut [u8]` slices with no heap allocations:

- `find_entry_in_block(slice, name) -> Option<u64>` — linear scan, string compare
- `find_entry_in_block_with_hash(slice, name, hash) -> Option<u64>` — hash filter then string compare
- `find_insert_offset_in_block(slice) -> usize` — finds first zero `name_len` (append position)
- `remove_entry_in_block_bytes(slice, name, hash) -> Option<u64>` — in-place compaction, zeros tail
- `has_valid_entry_in_block(slice) -> bool` — `fsck` helper
- `for_each_valid_inode_in_block(slice, f)` — `fsck` visitor over valid inode IDs
- `DirectoryIterator<'a>` — streaming deserializer over `&[u8]`

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/disk.rs] file "../src/disk.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
These are used by [`DiskManager::build_dir_index`](../src/disk.rs) and the directory cache to avoid per-entry allocations during cold scans.

## Directory cache and lookup flow

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/disk/caches.rs] file "../src/disk/caches.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
[`src/disk/caches.rs`](../src/disk/caches.rs) defines:

- **`DirIndex`**: Two `BTreeMap<String, ...>` maps:
  - `stored`: on-disk ciphertext name (with `_e_` prefix) → `(inode_id, block_id, stored_hash)`
  - `plain`: plaintext name → `(inode_id, plain_hash)` (only populated on encrypted filesystems)
  - `complete`: boolean, true when index represents the full directory (all blocks scanned)
  - `plain_complete`: boolean, true when `plain` map has all entries matching `stored`
  - `cold_scans`: counter of full-directory scans since last promotion
  - `may_have_holes`: true if removals created gaps usable for O(1) insert
  - `tail_offset`: `Option<(block_id, used_bytes)>` for fast appends when no holes

- **`ShardedDirCache`**: 32 shards (`ShardedDirCache::SHARDS = 32`), Fibonacci hash `inode_id.wrapping_mul(0x9e3779b97f4a7c15) >> 27` to select shard. Each shard guarded by `RwLock<BTreeMap<u64, DirIndex>>`.

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/disk.rs] file "../src/disk.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
### Lookup algorithm (`DiskManager::dir_lookup` in [`src/disk.rs`](../src/disk.rs))

1. **Cache hit**: Check shard for `parent_id`. If `encrypted`, probe `plain` map with plaintext name; else probe `stored` map. If `complete` (and `plain_complete` if encrypted), negative result is authoritative → return `None` immediately.
2. **Complete index miss**: If index exists and is `complete` but `plain_complete` is false (encrypted FS, first lookup after index built), scan on-disk blocks once to populate `plain` map.
3. **Cold scan → index build**: On first miss with no index, `build_dir_index` reads all directory blocks, decrypts filenames (if encrypted), builds complete `stored` and `plain` maps, promotes to `complete = true`, caches `tail_offset` for O(1) append.
4. **Targeted scan**: If index exists but not complete, scans only the block where the entry might reside (based on `tail_offset` or hole list).

After a successful lookup or insert, `plain` map is updated and `plain_complete` is set when `plain.len() == stored.len()`.

## Multi-block directory structure

Directories can span multiple 4 KiB blocks linked via the inode's `blocks[0..12]` (direct) and `triple_indirect` pointers. There is no separate directory block bitmap; the inode's block array is the authoritative list. `DiskManager::build_dir_index` iterates all block IDs in the inode (via `resolve_logical_block_id` for indirect blocks), reads each block, and parses entries until `name_len == 0` or block end.

## Key invariants and failure modes

| Invariant | Enforcement |
|-----------|-------------|
| Inode record is exactly 256 bytes, `record_version == 2` | `encode_v2` / `decode_v2`; padding bytes 171–255 must be zero |
| `mode` is only `File` (0) or `Directory` (1) | `decode_v2` validates discriminant |
| `blocks[0] == 0` for empty files/dirs | Caller convention; `allocate_block` never returns 0 |
| `encryption_nonce` is unique per file | `generate_nonce()` uses `OsRng` (24 bytes = 192 bits) |
| Directory entry `name_len ≤ 255` | `validate_filename` rejects longer names; `serialize_into` enforces |
| No path separators (`/`, `\`) or NUL in filenames | `validate_filename` |
| `.` and `..` never stored as directory entries | `validate_filename` rejects them; VFS synthesizes them |
| On encrypted FS, directory entries always store `_e_` ciphertext | `stored_filename` encrypts before write; `decrypt_filename_authenticated` rejects non-prefixed entries during scan |
| SIV nonce verification is constant-time | `ct_eq_slice` in `decrypt_filename_authenticated` |
| Legacy v1 filenames rejected on v2+ images (anti-downgrade) | `decrypt_filename_authenticated` checks `encryption_version >= ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_CONTEXT_BOUND` |
| DirIndex `complete` ⇔ all blocks scanned | `build_dir_index` sets `complete = true` after full scan |
| `plain_complete` ⇔ `plain.len() == stored.len()` | Updated after every lookup/insert on encrypted FS |

### Failure semantics

- `InodeFormatError::InvalidRecordVersion` → on-disk corruption or version mismatch
- `InodeFormatError::InvalidFileType` → `mode` not 0 or 1
- `InodeFormatError::NonZeroPadding` → bytes 171–255 not zero (tampering or v1 residue)
- `DirectoryError::EntryTooLarge` → `name_len > 255` on read or write
- `DirectoryError::InvalidFilename` → empty, `.`, `..`, contains `/`, `\`, or NUL
- `EncryptionError::DecryptionFailed` → Poly1305 tag mismatch, SIV nonce mismatch, Base64 decode error, or UTF-8 decode error
- `DiskManagerError::Io` → underlying block device error

## Extension points and configuration

| Feature | Configuration | Source |
|---------|---------------|--------|
<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/encryption.rs] file "../src/encryption.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
| Argon2id KDF parameters | `ARGON2_M_COST_KIB`, `ARGON2_T_COST`, `ARGON2_P_COST` constants in [`src/encryption.rs`](../src/encryption.rs) | OWASP / RFC 9106 defaults (64 MiB, 3, 4) |
<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/superblock.rs] file "../src/superblock.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
| Encryption scheme version | `superblock.encryption_version` (1 = legacy, 2 = context-bound) | [`src/superblock.rs`](../src/superblock.rs) |
<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/inode.rs] file "../src/inode.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
| Seekable 64 KiB chunk compression | `INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K = 0x01` in `Inode.flags` | [`src/inode.rs`](../src/inode.rs) |
<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/disk/caches.rs#L175] file "../src/disk/caches.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
| Directory cache promotion threshold | `DIR_INDEX_BUILD_AFTER_SCANS = 8` | [`src/disk/caches.rs`](../src/disk/caches.rs#L175) |
<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/disk/caches.rs#L202] file "../src/disk/caches.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/directory.rs#L5] file "../src/directory.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
