nodes.title: Filesystem Integrity Checking (fsck)
nodes.description: How the OIFS fsck structural consistency scanner performs set-theoretic verification between bitmap allocation states and directory reachability to detect orphan inodes, leaked blocks, missing blocks, and cross-linked blocks, plus read-only journal cleanliness verification. Covers chunk reference validation, deduplication detection, repair strategies, and verification flow.

nodes.title: Metadata WAL / Journaling
nodes.description: Describes the transactional metadata write-ahead log (WAL) that ensures crash resilience, including its circular buffer design, CRC32C protection, idempotent redo replay, JBD2-style deferred checkpointing under Strict durability, and DurabilityMode semantics.
nodes.body:
# Metadata WAL / Journaling

The journal subsystem implements a write-ahead log (WAL) for metadata mutations in OIFS. Before any metadata change (e.g., `create_file`, `delete_file`, `mkdir`, inode updates) is applied to the filesystem image, it is first recorded as a checksummed transaction in a fixed-size circular ring buffer residing in the journal region on disk. On crash recovery, the journal replays all durable-but-unapplied transactions to restore a consistent state, eliminating the need for a full `fsck` scan.

## Design Overview

* **Backward compatibility** – The on-disk `SuperBlock` layout is unchanged; a journaled image is identified by geometry (`inode_table_block >= 3 + JOURNAL_RESERVED_BLOCKS`) and a magic word in the journal header block. Non-journaled images behave exactly as before.
* **Idempotent redo** – Every `MetadataOp` encodes an absolute post-image write or an absolute bit-set operation. Replaying a transaction any number of times yields the same filesystem state, which makes the "write WAL first, then apply in place" approach safe even if a crash occurs during the in-place phase.
* **Torn-write detection** – Each transaction frame carries a CRC32C (Castagnoli) checksum over its header and payload, plus a trailing commit marker (`0xDEAD_BEEF`). A partially written frame fails verification and is ignored during recovery.
* **Zero new dependencies** – CRC32C is implemented in-crate with a compile-time generated table, keeping the code verifiable under model-checking tools like Kani/CBMC.
* **Mandatory journaling** – Every metadata mutation must go through the journal. Bypassing the journal leaves stale transactions in the ring; replay would overwrite newer changes with old post-images, causing silent data loss (observed when a zeroed inode post-image from a stalled `create` overwrote a later write's size and block pointers).

## On-Disk Layout

The journal region occupies the first `1 + JOURNAL_RING_BLOCKS` blocks of a journaled image:

| Block ID | Contents                          |
|----------|-----------------------------------|
| 3        | Journal header block (40 bytes of state + padding) |
| 4‑35     | Record ring (32 blocks = 128 KiB) |

* `JOURNAL_HEADER_MAGIC = 0x4A52_4E4C` ("JRNL" in ASCII)
* `JOURNAL_FORMAT_VERSION = 1`
* `JOURNAL_RING_BLOCKS = 32`
* `JOURNAL_RESERVED_BLOCKS = 33` (1 header + 32 ring blocks)
* `JOURNAL_INODE_TABLE_BLOCK = 36` (first inode-table block in a journaled image)

### Journal Header (40 bytes, little-endian)

| Offset | Size | Field               | Description |
|--------|------|---------------------|-------------|
| 0      | 4    | magic               | `JOURNAL_HEADER_MAGIC` |
| 4      | 4    | version             | `JOURNAL_FORMAT_VERSION` |
| 8      | 4    | ring_blocks         | `JOURNAL_RING_BLOCKS` |
| 12     | 8    | head                | Byte offset of next append position within the record ring |
| 20     | 8    | tail                | Byte offset of the oldest transaction still needing replay |
| 28     | 8    | tx_seq              | Monotonically increasing transaction sequence number |
| 36     | 1    | cleanly_unmounted   | `1` after a clean shutdown or successful recovery |
| 37‑39  | 3    | reserved            | Zero-filled |

### Transaction Frame Layout

Each transaction is stored as a contiguous frame inside the ring buffer:

| Field          | Size | Description |
|----------------|------|-------------|
| magic          | 4 B  | `TX_MAGIC = 0x5741_4C54` ("WALT") |
| tx_seq         | 8 B  | Transaction sequence number (matches header) |
| payload_len    | 4 B  | Length of the encoded metadata-operations payload |
| crc32c         | 4 B  | CRC32C over `tx_seq || payload_len || payload` |
| payload        | *    | Serialized `MetadataOp` sequence |
| commit_marker  | 4 B  | `TX_COMMIT_MARKER = 0xDEAD_BEEF` written **after** the payload |

The CRC covers everything except the leading magic and the marker itself, allowing the checksum to be stored inline while still detecting torn writes that corrupt any part of the protected region.

## Core Abstractions

### `JournalState`

Persisted in the journal header, tracks the ring buffer pointers and hygiene flag:

* `head` – next write offset (monotonic, wraps modulo ring size)
* `tail` – oldest un-checkpointed transaction offset
* `tx_seq` – latest transaction sequence number
* `cleanly_unmounted` – set after a clean unmount or successful recovery

### `MetadataOp`

Represents a single idempotent metadata mutation. Variants:

* `SetInodeBitmap` – allocate/free an inode
* `SetDataBitmap` – allocate/free a data block
* `SetDataBitmapRange` – allocate/free a contiguous range of data blocks
* `WriteInode` – overwrite a full 256-byte inode record (post-image)
* `WriteBlockSlice` – overwrite a byte range inside a data block (used for directory entry updates)

All encoding is little-endian, self-delimiting via a leading tag byte, and bounded in size (`encoded_size`).

### `JournalRing<'a>`

A mutable view over the journal region of a memory-mapped image. Provides the main operational interface:

* `open` – attach to an existing journal region, validating the header
* `create` – format a fresh empty journal
* `append` – encode and write a transaction, advancing `head` and handling wrap-around and overwrite-oldest semantics
* `persist` – flush the header block to stable storage (caller must `msync` the header plus the last written frame range)
* `recover` – replay all valid transactions between `tail` and `head` in order, stopping at the first torn or corrupt frame
* `checkpoint` / `checkpoint_to` – advance `tail` to discard transactions whose in-place effects are already durable

## Write-Ahead Logging Protocol

The journaling protocol follows a strict sequence for every metadata mutation:

1. **Stage operations** – The mutation's metadata effects are encoded as a `Vec<MetadataOp>` using `AllocSim` to predict allocator behavior without touching on-disk bitmaps. For data writes, small payloads (≤ 8 KiB) may be inlined as `WriteBlockSlice` ops directly in the frame under `DurabilityMode::Strict`.
2. **Encode transaction frame** – `encode_frame` coalesces adjacent operations (e.g., contiguous `SetDataBitmap` → `SetDataBitmapRange`, contiguous `WriteBlockSlice` → single slice) and builds a CRC32C-protected frame with sequence number, payload length, payload, and commit marker.
3. **Append to ring and persist** – `JournalRing::append` writes the frame contiguously (wrapping to offset 0 if needed), updates `head`, increments `tx_seq`, clears `cleanly_unmounted`, and persists the header. The caller receives the byte range written (`last_write`) and any wrap-zeroed tail range (`last_wrap_pad`).
4. **Apply in place** – The same `MetadataOp` list is applied to the live image via `apply_op_in_place`, which performs absolute post-image writes to bitmaps, inode table, and data blocks. Because every op is an absolute assignment, re-applying a committed transaction is idempotent.
5. **Checkpoint (deferred)** – Once the in-place writes are known durable, the journal ring is advanced via `checkpoint_to` (using a `head` snapshot taken before the flush) or `checkpoint` (tail := head). This discards the WAL record and frees ring space. Under `DurabilityMode::Strict`, checkpointing occurs automatically when the ring reaches 50% capacity; under `Lazy`, `RangeAsync`, and `LegacyWholeMmapAsync`, the ring is kept and mount-time recovery replays it.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Metadata Mutation] --> B[Stage MetadataOps via AllocSim]
    B --> C[Encode Frame with CRC32C]
    C --> D[Append to Ring Buffer]
    D --> E[Persist Header + Frame to Storage]
    E --> F[Apply Ops In-Place]
    F --> G{DurabilityMode?}
    G -->|Strict| H[Flush In-Place Ranges]
    G -->|RangeAsync| I[Accumulate Dirty Ranges]
    G -->|Lazy| J[No Immediate Flush]
    H --> K[Checkpoint When Ring ≥ 50%]
    I --> L[Batch msync on Threshold]
    J --> M[Mount-Time Recovery Replays]
    K --> N[Ring Space Freed]
    L --> M
    M --> N
```

## CRC32C Verification

* **Algorithm** – Castagnoli polynomial (`0x82F6_3B78`) with standard reflected representation, pre- and post-inversion (`!crc32c_update(0xFFFF_FFFF, data)`).
* **Hardware acceleration** – Uses ARMv8 CRC extension (`__crc32cb`/`__crc32cd`) or x86 SSE4.2 (`_mm_crc32_u64`/`_mm_crc32_u8`) when available; falls back to a `const fn` software table (256-entry) generated at compile time. The same function is used on all paths, making results deterministic for Kani/CBMC proofs.
* **Coverage** – The checksum is computed over `tx_seq || payload_len || payload`. The leading magic (`TX_MAGIC`) and trailing commit marker (`TX_COMMIT_MARKER`) are excluded so the checksum field itself can be stored inline.
* **Validation** – `decode_frame` verifies magic, payload length bounds, CRC32C match, and commit marker presence. A frame that fails any check is treated as torn; recovery stops at the first invalid frame and replays everything before it.

## Redo Recovery

On mount, `DiskManager::recover_journal` performs three phases:

1. **Snapshot & decode** – The journal region is copied to a local buffer. `JournalRing::recover` walks from `tail` to `head`, validating each frame with `decode_frame`. Valid frames are collected; the first invalid frame stops the scan.
2. **Redo apply** – Collected `MetadataOp`s are applied in order to the live image via `apply_op_in_place`. Idempotence guarantees that replaying a partially applied transaction is safe.
3. **Ring reset** – The header is rewritten with `head = 0`, `tail = 0`, `cleanly_unmounted = true`, and the header block is flushed. Subsequent mounts see a clean journal.

Recovery is automatic and requires no user intervention. The `cleanly_unmounted` flag in the header also allows a fast path: if the flag is set and the ring is empty, mount skips the scan entirely.

## Checkpointing

Checkpointing discards WAL entries whose in-place effects are already durable, freeing ring capacity.

* **`JournalRing::checkpoint`** – Sets `tail := head`. After this, `used() == 0` and a subsequent `recover()` replays nothing.
* **`JournalRing::checkpoint_to(cursor)`** – Advances `tail` to `cursor` (a previous `head` snapshot), provided `cursor` lies between the old `tail` and `head` in ring order. The tail only moves forward and never passes `head`.
* **JBD2-style deferred checkpointing** – Under `DurabilityMode::Strict`, `DiskManager::maybe_checkpoint` is called after each mutation. It opens the journal region, checks if `ring.used() >= ring.ring_bytes() / 2`, and if so, flushes the entire image (`backing.flush()`) then calls `checkpoint_journal` (which calls `ring.checkpoint()` and flushes the header). This batches multiple transactions into a single `msync(MS_SYNC)` for the in-place metadata.
* **Other durability modes** – `Lazy`, `RangeAsync`, and `LegacyWholeMmapAsync` do **not** checkpoint on mutation. The ring accumulates until it wraps (overwrite-oldest semantics). Mount-time recovery will replay any un-checkpointed transactions. This is safe because the ring overwrites oldest-first, bounding journal size.

## Interaction with `DurabilityMode`

| Mode | WAL Frame Flush | In-Place Flush | Checkpointing |
|------|----------------|----------------|---------------|
| **Strict** | Synchronous `msync(MS_SYNC)` of frame + header on every `commit_journal_tx` (or batched via group-commit drainer) | Synchronous `msync(MS_SYNC)` of all mutated ranges on every mutation | Automatic at 50% ring watermark; also on explicit `flush()`/`Drop` |
| **RangeAsync** | Asynchronous `msync(MS_ASYNC)` of frame + header | Accumulated in `pending_async_ranges`, drained in coalesced batches (gap-bridged to 1 MiB) at threshold | **Never** on mutation; ring kept for recovery |
| **Lazy** | No per-mutation flush (relies on OS page cache) | No per-mutation flush | **Never** on mutation; ring kept for recovery |
| **LegacyWholeMmapAsync** | Asynchronous `msync(MS_ASYNC)` of entire mapping | Same as `RangeAsync` but whole mapping | **Never** on mutation; ring kept for recovery |

### Strict Mode Detail

In `Strict` mode, `commit_journal_tx` uses `JournalRing::try_append_without_overwrite`. If the ring lacks space for the new frame without overwriting un-checkpointed entries, it:
1. Flushes all pending in-place metadata (`guard.backing.flush()`)
2. Checkpoints the journal (`checkpoint_journal`)
3. Retries the append (now guaranteed to succeed on the empty ring)

This ensures the WAL never overwrites a transaction whose in-place effects are not yet durable.

The `is_strict_sync_deferred()` flag (controlled by a global group-commit batching state) modifies this: when `true`, the per-mutation synchronous flush is skipped and a background drainer issues a single `flush()` for the whole batch before completing any future. In that case, small payloads (≤ 8 KiB) are written directly to the data area instead of being inlined into the WAL frame, reducing ring pressure.

## AllocSim: Allocation Simulation

`AllocSim` predicts the on-disk allocator's behavior during transaction staging without modifying the live bitmaps:

* **`new_data_only`** – Used by `write_data`, `create_entry_journaled`, and other data-only mutations. It copies only the data bitmap (lazily, on first allocation/free) and tracks fresh block allocations, frees, and pointer updates in memory.
* **`new` (test-only)** – Copies both inode and data bitmaps for full mutation simulation.
* **Fresh block tracking** – Every allocated block is recorded in `fresh_blocks` and `unzeroed_fresh`. The transaction builder emits `WriteBlockSlice` ops to zero the block if it contains stale data.
* **Pointer simulation** – Indirect block pointer modifications are recorded in a `FxHashMap<(parent_block, slot), child_block>` so the transaction can encode the correct post-image pointer values.

When the transaction commits, the `MetadataOp` list contains `SetDataBitmap`/`SetDataBitmapRange` for the bitmap changes and `WriteBlockSlice` for zeroing/initializing fresh blocks, plus `WriteInode` for the updated inode.

## Journal Region Geometry

The `SuperBlock` method `has_journal_layout()` detects a journaled image:

* **Legacy layouts (v1/v2)** – Fixed geometry: `inode_table_block == 36` (`JOURNAL_INODE_TABLE_BLOCK`), meaning the journal header is at block 3 and the ring occupies blocks 4–35.
* **v3 layout** – Multi-block bitmaps; the journal region sits between the data bitmap and the inode table. `journal_header_block()` returns `data_bitmap_block + data_bitmap_blocks()`, and the ring follows. `has_journal_layout()` checks `inode_table_block == 1 + inode_bitmap_blocks + data_bitmap_blocks + JOURNAL_RESERVED_BLOCKS`.

This design keeps the `SuperBlock` binary layout identical for journaled and non-journaled images; the journal region is purely a geometry shift.

## Recovery Guarantees

* **No full `fsck` required** – Mount-time recovery replays only the durable tail of the WAL. A clean unmount (`mark_clean_shutdown` or `checkpoint`) leaves `cleanly_unmounted = true` and an empty ring, allowing a fast mount.
* **Torn frame isolation** – A power loss during frame write leaves a partial frame without a valid CRC or commit marker. Recovery stops at that frame; all earlier transactions are complete and are replayed. The partial frame is silently dropped.
* **Idempotent redo** – Because every `MetadataOp` is an absolute post-image assignment, applying a transaction twice has the same effect as applying it once. This makes the "WAL first, then in-place" protocol safe even if the crash occurs mid-way through the in-place phase.
* **Stale transaction prevention** – The requirement that **every** metadata mutation go through the journal prevents stale WAL entries from rolling back newer changes. If a mutation bypasses the journal while a stale transaction remains in the ring, recovery would replay the stale post-image over the newer on-disk state, causing silent data loss.

## Testing and Verification

* **Kani proofs** – `journal.rs` contains `#[kani::proof]` modules verifying:
  * Ring cursor arithmetic never leaves the ring
  * `checkpoint` empties the ring (`used() == 0`)
  * `checkpoint_to` monotonicity (tail never moves backward, never passes head)
  * `push_data_bitmap_op` never merges opposite-polarity spans
  * State-transition invariants of `append` (wrap handling, tail advancement)
* **Unit tests** – `checkpoint_tests` and integration tests cover:
  * Checkpoint advances tail to snapshot, leaves later transactions pending
  * Checkpoint never moves tail backwards
  * Checkpoint refuses cursors past head
  * Checkpointed transactions are not replayed on reopen
  * Ring wrap after checkpoint replays post-wrap frames
  * Ring wrap preserves pre-wrap un-checkpointed frames
  * Recovery stops at torn frame
  * `apply_op_in_place` is idempotent
* **Crash simulation** – `tests/crash_safety.rs` uses a fault-injecting backend to verify that after simulated power loss at any point, mount recovery produces a consistent filesystem.

## Related Pages

* [Disk Manager and Persistence](../architecture/disk_manager_and_persistence.md) – Durability modes, flush semantics, and journal interaction
* [Superblock and Layout](../architecture/superblock_and_layout.md) – Journal region geometry and `has_journal_layout()`
* [Crash Safety Testing](../testing/crash_safety_testing.md) – Fault injection and recovery verification

nodes.title: MCP Server (oifs_mcp)
nodes.description: How the oifs_mcp binary exposes the OIFS storage engine as Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools over stdio, providing AI agents with an isolated, single-file virtual filesystem for persistent memory.
nodes.body:
## Responsibility and ownership

The [`oifs_mcp`](repo://src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs) binary exposes the OIFS filesystem engine to AI agents (such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, and autonomous agent loops) via the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**.

Rather than giving AI agents unrestricted access to the host operating system filesystem, `oifs_mcp` provisions a self-contained, sandboxed `.img` container. All file operations, directory hierarchies, append logs, and storage metrics are fully confined within this single file image.

## Architecture and framework (rmcp)

`oifs_mcp` is built on top of [`rmcp`](repo://src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs#L10-L13) (the Rust MCP SDK), implementing an asynchronous JSON-RPC protocol over standard input/output (`stdio`):

<!-- openwiki: mermaid parse failed and this diagram was converted to a text fence so it does not break rendering. Fix the diagram source and restore the mermaid fence. Parser error: Parse error on line 2: ... A[AI Agent Host (Cursor / Claude Des Expecting 'SQE', 'DOUBLECIRCLEEND', 'PE', '-)', 'STADIUMEND', 'SUBROUTINEEND', 'PIPE', 'CYLINDEREND', 'DIAMOND_STOP', 'TAGEND', 'TRAPEND', 'INVTRAPEND', 'UNICODE_TEXT', 'TEXT', 'TAGSTART', got 'PS' -->
```text
flowchart TD
    A[AI Agent Host (Cursor / Claude Desktop)] -->|JSON-RPC (stdio transport)| B[rmcp Service Handler (ServerHandler)]
    B -->|ToolRouter dispatch & JsonSchema validation| C[OifsMcpServer]
    C -->|spawn_blocking| D[DiskManager (sync mmap I/O)]
    D -->|mmap & storage calls| E[OIFS Engine (DiskManager / Inode / Bitmap)]
```

### The OifsMcpServer structure

Server state is encapsulated by [`OifsMcpServer`](repo://src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs#L36-L43):

```rust
#[derive(Clone)]
struct OifsMcpServer {
    dm: DiskManager,
    append_lock: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<()>>,
    image_path: PathBuf,
    tool_router: ToolRouter<Self>,
}
```

- **Async–sync bridge**: Because `rmcp` operates in an asynchronous Tokio runtime while `DiskManager` performs synchronous mmap I/O, each tool handler offloads the synchronous `DiskManager` work to a blocking task via `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. The `DiskManager` itself is stored directly (not wrapped in a mutex) because each blocking task gets its own clone of the struct, and `DiskManager` uses internal `RwLock`/`Mutex` for its own synchronization.
- **Append serialization**: An additional `append_lock: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<()>>` serializes concurrent `append_file` calls so that multiple agents appending to the same log file interleave cleanly line-by-line.
- **Bootstrapping**: Constructed via [`OifsMcpServer::new`](repo://src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs#L45-L61). If the target image file does not yet exist and an `OIFS_PASSWORD` environment variable is detected, it automatically initializes an encrypted image via `DiskManager::create_encrypted`; otherwise, it calls `DiskManager::open_with_password`.
- **Defaults**: Defaults to `agent_memory.img` with a default size of 10 MB ([`DEFAULT_IMAGE`](repo://src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs#L23), [`DEFAULT_SIZE_MB`](repo://src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs#L24)), configurable via `--size <MB>` and positional CLI arguments.

## Server capabilities and initialization

The server implements [`ServerHandler`](repo://src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs#L370-L386) to announce capabilities during the MCP handshake:

```rust
#[rmcp::tool_handler]
impl ServerHandler for OifsMcpServer {
    fn get_info(&self) -> ServerInfo {
        ServerInfo {
            instructions: Some(
                "OIFS Memory Sandbox — A sandboxed inode filesystem for AI agent memory. \
                 All reads/writes are isolated inside a .img file."
                    .into(),
            ),
            capabilities: ServerCapabilities::builder().enable_tools().build(),
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }
}
```

By enabling `.enable_tools()`, the server advertises its available tool registry and JSON schemas to connected LLMs.

## Single-image sandbox model and path resolution

The sandbox model is deliberately simple:

1. **One image per server process**: The CLI accepts a single image path (default: `agent_memory.img`). All tools operate exclusively within this image.
2. **Path resolution is always relative to the image root**: Paths like `"notes/todo.txt"` or `"."` are resolved by `DiskManager::resolve_path` ([`disk.rs#L6704`](repo://src/disk.rs#L6704)) starting from the root inode (inode 1). There is no concept of "current working directory" — every path is absolute within the sandbox.
3. **Parent directories must exist**: `write_file`, `mkdir`, and `append_file` use `resolve_parent` ([`disk.rs#L6840`](repo://src/disk.rs#L6840)) to locate the parent directory inode, then create the child. They do **not** auto-create intermediate directories (no `mkdir -p` semantics). The agent must create the directory hierarchy first with `mkdir` calls.
4. **Encryption is image-scoped**: If `OIFS_PASSWORD` is set at startup, the entire image is encrypted with AES-256-XTS. The same password must be supplied on every subsequent launch to open the image. The MCP server itself has no key-management logic — it simply forwards the environment variable to `DiskManager`.

## Session management and DiskManager integration

The MCP server does **not** use `OifsSession` from [`session.rs`](repo://src/session.rs). Instead, it constructs `DiskManager` directly via `DiskManager::open_with_password` or `DiskManager::create_encrypted`, which operates in **Standalone mode** (direct `mmap` access, zero IPC overhead).

- The `OifsSession` abstraction in `session.rs` provides a process-wide registry and supports three modes (`Standalone`, `Local` UDS IPC, `Network` TCP). The MCP server bypasses this entirely and holds a `DiskManager` directly.
- This means there is **no cross-process session sharing** for the MCP server — each `oifs_mcp` process has its own independent `DiskManager` handle to the image file. If multiple agent hosts need shared access, the IPC/daemon path ([`src/ipc.rs`](repo://src/ipc.rs)) or FUSE mount ([`src/fuse.rs`](repo://src/fuse.rs)) should be used instead.

## Available MCP tools

All tools are registered via the [`tool_router`](repo://src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs#L123) macro. Each tool clones `self.dm`, executes the operation inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, and returns a JSON string built with `serde_json` (never hand-rolled `format!`) to guarantee correct escaping.

### Tool response convention

- **Success**: `{"ok": true, ...}` with tool-specific fields.
- **Error**: `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}`.

### write_file

```json
{
  "name": "write_file",
  "description": "Write (create or overwrite) a file inside the OIFS sandbox image. Parent directories must already exist.",
  "parameters": { "path": "string", "content": "string" }
}
```

- Resolves parent directory via `resolve_parent`, creates file if missing via `create_file`, then writes content via `write_data_truncated` with `CompressionMode::Auto` ([`disk.rs#L8053`](repo://src/disk.rs#L8053)).
- Returns `{"ok": true, "inode": <u64>, "bytes": <usize>}`.

### read_file

```json
{
  "name": "read_file",
  "description": "Read the contents of a file inside the OIFS sandbox image. Returns UTF-8 text content.",
  "parameters": { "path": "string" }
}
```

- Resolves path via `resolve_path`, reads data via `read_data` ([`disk.rs#L4741`](repo://src/disk.rs#L4741)), validates UTF-8.
- Returns raw UTF-8 string content on success (not JSON-wrapped), or JSON error object on failure.

### list_dir

```json
{
  "name": "list_dir",
  "description": "List files and directories at a given path inside the OIFS sandbox image. Returns one JSON object per line (JSONL).",
  "parameters": { "path": "string" }
}
```

- Resolves directory inode via `resolve_path`, reads entries via `list_dir` ([`disk.rs#L6721`](repo://src/disk.rs#L6721)), reads each child inode for type and size.
- Returns **JSONL** (newline-delimited JSON objects): each line is `{"name": "...", "kind": "file|dir", "size": <u64>}`. Empty directory returns `{"entries":0}`.

### mkdir

```json
{
  "name": "mkdir",
  "description": "Create a directory inside the OIFS sandbox image. Parent directories must exist.",
  "parameters": { "path": "string" }
}
```

- Resolves parent via `resolve_parent`, creates directory via `create_directory` ([`disk.rs#L4076`](repo://src/disk.rs#L4076)).
- Returns `{"ok": true, "inode": <u64>}`.

### delete_file

```json
{
  "name": "delete_file",
  "description": "Delete a file from the OIFS sandbox image.",
  "parameters": { "path": "string" }
}
```

- Resolves parent via `resolve_parent`, deletes via `delete_file` ([`disk.rs#L7244`](repo://src/disk.rs#L7244)).
- Returns `{"ok": true}`.

### truncate_file

```json
{
  "name": "truncate_file",
  "description": "Truncate or extend a file in the OIFS sandbox image to the specified size in bytes.",
  "parameters": { "path": "string", "size": "u64" }
}
```

- Truncates via `truncate_path` ([`disk.rs#L8044`](repo://src/disk.rs#L8044)).
- Returns `{"ok": true, "size": <u64>}`.

### append_file

```json
{
  "name": "append_file",
  "description": "Append a line to a file inside the OIFS sandbox image. Creates the file if it does not exist. Ideal for JSONL memory logs.",
  "parameters": { "path": "string", "content": "string" }
}
```

- Acquires `append_lock` (process-wide `std::sync::Mutex<()>`) to serialize concurrent appends.
- Resolves parent via `resolve_parent`, creates file if missing via `create_file`, then appends via `write_data` at current file size with `CompressionMode::Never` ([`disk.rs#L5279`](repo://src/disk.rs#L5279)). Ensures trailing newline.
- Returns `{"ok": true, "inode": <u64>, "total_bytes": <u64>}`.

### status

```json
{
  "name": "status",
  "description": "Show filesystem status: image path, total/used/free blocks, and fragmentation ratio."
}
```

- Calls `analyze_fragmentation` ([`disk.rs#L147`](repo://src/disk.rs#L147)).
- Returns `{"image": "...", "total_blocks": <u64>, "used_blocks": <u64>, "free_blocks": <u64>, "fragmentation": <f64>}`.

## MCP tool invocation flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent as AI Agent (Cursor/Claude)
    participant Transport as stdio (JSON-RPC)
    participant Handler as rmcp ServerHandler
    participant Router as ToolRouter
    participant Server as OifsMcpServer
    participant Blocking as tokio::spawn_blocking
    participant DM as DiskManager

    Agent->>Transport: tools/call {name, arguments}
    Transport->>Handler: JSON-RPC request
    Handler->>Router: Dispatch by tool name
    Router->>Server: Call typed handler (e.g. write_file)
    Server->>Blocking: spawn_blocking(move || { dm.op(...) })
    Blocking->>DM: Synchronous mmap I/O
    DM-->>Blocking: Result
    Blocking-->>Server: Result<String>
    Server-->>Router: JSON response string
    Router-->>Handler: CallResult
    Handler-->>Transport: JSON-RPC response
    Transport-->>Agent: Result or error
```

## CLI startup behavior

The [`main`](repo://src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs#L388-L444) function:

1. Parses CLI arguments: optional `--size <MB>` (default 10), optional positional `IMAGE_PATH` (default `agent_memory.img`).
2. Computes `size_bytes = size_mb * 1024 * 1024` with `checked_mul` to prevent overflow.
3. Reads `OIFS_PASSWORD` from environment.
4. Logs: `[oifs-mcp] image=<path> size=<MB> encrypted=<bool>`.
5. Constructs `OifsMcpServer::new(image_path, size_bytes, password)`.
6. Starts rmcp stdio service: `server.serve(rmcp::transport::stdio()).await?`.
7. Waits for service to complete: `service.waiting().await?`.

### Image creation / open logic

```rust
let dm = match (!image_path.exists(), password) {
    (true, Some(pwd)) => DiskManager::create_encrypted(&image_path, size_bytes, pwd)?,
    _ => DiskManager::open_with_password(&image_path, size_bytes, password)?,
};
```

- **New image + password set** → `create_encrypted` (AES-256-XTS encrypted image).
- **New image, no password** → `open_with_password` creates a plain (unencrypted) image.
- **Existing image + password** → `open_with_password` opens encrypted image (verifies password).
- **Existing image, no password** → `open_with_password` opens plain image.

## What the MCP server does NOT expose

- **No MCP resources**: The server does not implement `resources/list`, `resources/read`, or resource templates. All filesystem access is mediated exclusively through the eight registered tools.
- **No prompts**: No prompt templates are registered.
- **No sampling**: No `sampling/createMessage` support.

## Related pages

- [MCP Integration](../integrations/mcp_integration.md) — configuring Cursor, Claude Desktop, and other MCP clients.
- [CLI Reference](../operations/cli_reference.md) — full CLI options for `oifs_mcp` and other binaries.
- [MCP Workflow](../workflows/mcp_workflow.md) — end-to-end agent memory workflows using the MCP server.

nodes.title: Architecture Overview
nodes.description: High-level system map showing owned subsystems, runtime domains, and cross-system data flows for OIFS.
nodes.body:
# Architecture Overview OIFS (O's Inode File System) is a high-performance, embedded, multi-process inode filesystem engine implemented in Rust. It delivers crash-resilient storage, fine-grained concurrency, military-grade AEAD encryption, scientific data pre-compression filters, pluggable asynchronous I/O engines, a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agents, a zero-external-C-dependency FUSE kernel protocol implementation (ABI v7.28), a stable C/C++ FFI interface, a pure-Rust NFSv3 loopback server, and cross-image fast transfer/splice/cloning capabilities — all packaged in a single portable `.img` container file. > 🌐 **Interactive Architecture & Specs**: [https://ych.github.io/oifs/](https://ych.github.io/oifs/) > 📦 **Source Repository**: [https://github.com/ych/oifs](https://github.com/ych/oifs) ## System Context Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Clients["Client Interfaces"] RustAPI["Rust API
`DiskManager`, `OifsSession`, `OifsAsyncTask`"] CFFI["C/C++ FFI
`oifs.h` / `oifs.hpp` / `co_await`"] FUSE["Pure-Rust FUSE
ABI v7.28 Linux/macOS"] NFS["Pure-Rust NFSv3
Loopback TCP Mount"] CLI["CLI Tool
`oifs` binary"] MCP["MCP Server
`oifs_mcp` for AI Agents"] end subgraph Coordination["Multi-Process Coordination"] Session["Session Registry
`OifsSession` (Direct/Remote)"] IPC["IPC Transport
UDS Local / TCP Network
Active Ping Probe"] end subgraph Engine["Storage Engine (DiskManager)"] Cache["Inode & Dir Caches
32-shard Fibonacci Hash"] Pipeline["Out-of-Lock Pipeline
Delta/Shuffle/BitShuffle → Zstd → XChaCha20-Poly1305"] Transfer["3-Tier Cross-Image Transfer
Reflink → copy_file_range → Raw Blocks"] WAL["Metadata WAL Journal
CRC32C, 128 KiB Ring, Ordered Mode"] Defrag["Auto Defrag Coordinator
WAL-atomic In-Place Defrag"] end subgraph Storage["Dual Storage Engine (Single .img Container)"] Mmap["StorageMode::Mmap
memmap2::MmapMut
Zero-Copy MAP_SHARED"] MmapRO["StorageMode::MmapReadOnly
memmap2::Mmap
PROT_READ Only"] FileIo["StorageMode::FileIo
pread/pwrite + 64-shard
DataPageCache + 16-shard MetadataCache"] end Clients --> Session Session --> IPC Session --> Engine IPC --> Engine Engine --> Cache Cache --> Pipeline Cache --> Transfer Pipeline --> WAL WAL --> Storage Transfer --> Storage Defrag -.-> WAL Defrag -.-> Engine ``` *Diagram: OIFS system context showing client interfaces, coordination layer, storage engine pipeline, and dual storage backends.* --- ## Core Design Principles | Principle | Description | |-----------|-------------| | **Single-Image Container** | All filesystem metadata (superblock, inodes, directories, bitmaps, WAL journal) and file data stored contiguously in one host file. | | **Block-Oriented Layout** | Fixed 4 KiB block size with extent-based indexing (direct, single/double/triple indirect) supports files up to 513 GB. | | **Pluggable I/O Engine** | Decouples payload block access from memory mapping via configurable backends: `Mmap` (default), `Pread`, Linux `io_uring`. | | **Multi-Process Concurrency** | Dynamic Master-Proxy architecture coordinates shared access via IPC (Unix Domain Sockets or TCP with Active Ping Probe). | --- ## Storage Engines OIFS supports three storage engine modes over the exact same on-disk format. The mode is selected at open time via [`StorageMode`][repo://src/storage.rs#L140-L155] and persists for the lifetime of the `DiskManager` handle. ### 1. `StorageMode::Mmap` (Default) — Zero-Copy Memory Mapping ```rust // src/storage.rs:140-155 pub enum StorageMode { /// Memory-mapped container (memmap2::MmapMut, default). #[default] Mmap = 0, /// Pure positional pread/pwrite I/O without calling mmap(). FileIo = 1, } ``` - **Implementation**: [`ImageBacking::Mmap`][repo://src/storage.rs#L940-L1050] wraps `memmap2::MmapMut` with `MAP_SHARED`, giving direct zero-copy access to the entire `.img` file. - **Read Path**: `mmap_slice()` returns `&[u8]` directly; inode records for format v2+ are decoded in-place from the mapping without additional copies. - **Write Path**: Mutations modify the shared mapping; dirty pages are flushed according to [`DurabilityMode`][repo://src/disk.rs#L380-L430] (`Lazy`/`RangeAsync`/`Strict`/`LegacyWholeMmapAsync`). - **Performance**: 40–58 GB/s on resident pages; batch reads resolve double-indirect extents by coalescing 4 KiB pages into large extents. - **Crash Safety**: `MAP_SHARED` ensures modifications survive process crashes (SIGKILL); power-loss resilience depends on `DurabilityMode` and explicit `flush()`. ### 2. `StorageMode::MmapReadOnly` — Read-Only Memory Mapping - **Implementation**: [`ImageBacking::MmapReadOnly`][repo://src/storage.rs#L1050-L1120] uses `memmap2::Mmap` with `PROT_READ` only. - **Use Case**: `DiskManager::open_read_only*()` constructors for inspection of `0444` images. - **Concurrency**: Acquires shared advisory lock (`F_RDLCK`), allowing multiple simultaneous readers while excluding writers (`F_WRLCK`). - **WAL Verification**: On journaled images, verifies zero unrecovered transactions with zero disk writes. - **Zero Flush on Drop**: Read-only mounts suppress all `msync`/`fdatasync` in `Drop`. ### 3. `StorageMode::FileIo` — Zero-mmap Positional I/O ```rust // src/storage.rs:1120-1400 pub(crate) struct FileBacking { file: File, len: usize, read_only: bool, inode_bitmap_off: u64, inode_bitmap: Vec, // Write-through mirror data_bitmap_off: u64, data_bitmap: Vec, // Write-through mirror journal_off: u64, journal_buf: Vec, // In-memory WAL mirror block_cache: MetadataBlockCache, // 16-shard, 4 MiB data_cache: DataPageCache, // 64-shard, 32 MiB default } ``` - **Read Path**: `pread(2)` for all I/O; metadata blocks (indirect pointers, directory blocks) cached in **16-shard MetadataBlockCache** (4 MiB total); data blocks cached in **64-shard DataPageCache** (32 MiB default, configurable via `OIFS_FILE_IO_CACHE_MB`). - **Write Path**: `pwrite(2)` with **write-through mirrors** for bitmaps and WAL region; cache invalidation on write (`update_if_present` for small spans, `invalidate_block_range` for large streaming writes). - **Cache Coherency**: Second-Chance Clock eviction for data cache; metadata cache uses Fibonacci hash sharding. Both are strictly coherent on every write, zero, copy, and WAL replay. - **Scan Resistance**: Extents > 64 KiB bypass `DataPageCache` to preserve sequential throughput. - **Safety**: 100% Safe Rust; eliminates `SIGBUS` crashes and `unsafe` memory-mapping hazards. - **I/O Backend**: [`IoBackend::Pread`][repo://src/io_engine.rs#L1-L50] (default) or `IoBackend::IoUring` (Linux, `--features io_uring`). --- ## Dual-Layer Cache Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Mmap["StorageMode::Mmap"] MMAP_INODE["Inode Cache\n(Bounded, 32-shard)\n~128 KiB entries"] MMAP_DIR["Dir Cache\n(Sharded, 32-shard)\nDirectoryEntry vecs"] MMAP_CHUNK["Chunk Read Cache\nSeekable 64K chunks\n16-shard, 128 entries"] MMAP_BLOB["Decoded Blob Cache\nNon-seekable Zstd\n16-shard, 32 entries"] end subgraph FileIo["StorageMode::FileIo"] FI_META["MetadataBlockCache\n16-shard, 4 KiB blocks\n4 MiB total"] FI_DATA["DataPageCache\n64-shard, 4 KiB pages\n32 MiB default\nSecond-Chance Clock"] FI_INODE["Inode Cache\n(if format v1)\nSame as Mmap"] FI_DIR["Dir Cache\nSame as Mmap"] end style Mmap fill:#e8f5e9 style FileIo fill:#e3f2fd ``` | Cache Layer | Mmap | FileIo | Purpose | |-------------|------|--------|---------| | **Inode Cache** | ✅ 32-shard | ✅ (v1 inodes only) | Zero-copy metadata access | | **Dir Cache** | ✅ 32-shard | ✅ | Path resolution acceleration | | **Chunk Read Cache** | ✅ 16-shard | ✅ | Seekable 64K chunk decompression | | **Decoded Blob Cache** | ✅ 16-shard | ✅ | Full-file Zstd stream caching | | **Metadata Block Cache** | ❌ (direct mmap) | ✅ 16-shard, 4 MiB | Indirect ptr / dir block caching | | **Data Page Cache** | ❌ (OS page cache) | ✅ 64-shard, 32 MiB | Hot random/small-file reads | **Key Invariant**: Under `Mmap` with format v2+ inodes, the inode cache is **bypassed entirely** — inodes are decoded directly from the mapping via [`uses_direct_mmap_inode`][repo://src/disk.rs#L650-L660]. --- ## Core Subsystems ### DiskManager — Central Storage Engine [`DiskManager`][repo://src/disk.rs#L1-L100] is the primary entrypoint owning the `.img` file, superblock, bitmaps, inode table, and WAL journal. Key responsibilities: | Responsibility | Implementation | |----------------|----------------| | **File/Directory CRUD** | `create_file`, `create_directory`, `delete_file`, `lookup`, `rename` | | **Data I/O** | `read_data`, `read_at`, `write_data`, `write_data_with_filters`, `truncate` | | **Compression Pipeline** | SIMD Delta/Shuffle/BitShuffle → Seekable 64K Zstd / Stream Zstd (out-of-lock) | | **Encryption** | XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (payload), BLAKE2b-512 SIV + XChaCha20-Poly1305 (filenames) | | **Metadata WAL** | CRC32C 128 KiB ring buffer, ordered mode, deferred checkpoint | | **Cross-Image Transfer** | 3-tier: `FICLONERANGE`/`clonefile` → `copy_file_range` → Raw block copy | | **Defragmentation** | Safe (new image) and WAL-atomic in-place modes | | **Integrity Check** | `verify_integrity()` — full fsck (orphans, leaks, cross-links, missing blocks) | | **Format Migration** | In-place v1→v2 inode record upgrade with resumable cursor | **Concurrency**: Single `RwLock` protecting all mutable state; read-heavy operations (batch reads, lookups) take shared locks; mutations take exclusive lock with out-of-lock CPU-intensive pipeline (filter/compress/encrypt). ### Session — Master-Proxy Coordination [`OifsSession`][repo://src/session.rs#L1-L100] provides transparent multi-process access via three modes: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Standalone: open() / get_or_open() Standalone --> Local: open_local() / --ipc Standalone --> Network: open_network() / --network Local --> Standalone: Last proxy exits Network --> Standalone: Master exits state Standalone { [*] --> DirectMmap DirectMmap: Direct DiskManager access\nZero IPC overhead } state Local { [*] --> Master: First opener [*] --> Proxy: Subsequent openers Master --> Proxy: UDS in /tmp\nOwner-only 0700 dir Proxy --> Master: Transparent IPC forward\nAuto-reconnect on master exit } state Network { [*] --> Master: First opener [*] --> Proxy: Subsequent openers Master --> Proxy: .image.master rendezvous\nTCP + Clock-Free Active Ping Probe Proxy --> Master: Challenge-response auth\nAuto-failover to local master } ``` | Mode | Transport | Auth | Use Case | |------|-----------|------|----------| | **Standalone** | None (direct) | N/A | Single-process, CLI, embedded | | **Local** | Unix Domain Socket (`/tmp`) | Session secret (owner-only `0700` dir) | Multi-process same machine | | **Network** | TCP + `.image.master` rendezvous | Challenge-response (BLAKE2b-512) | NFS/Lustre/multi-node clusters | **Failover**: Proxies automatically reconnect on master exit; if a proxy becomes the new master (via `bind_or_connect` race), it promotes its `DiskManager` and starts an `IpcServer` seamlessly. ### Encryption Subsystem [`encryption.rs`][repo://src/encryption.rs#L1-L100] implements a hardened key hierarchy: ``` Argon2id (m=64 MiB, t=3, p=4) + salt │ ▼ Master Key (256-bit) │ ├─► BLAKE2b-512(KDF_CONTEXT_PAYLOAD) ──► Payload Key: XChaCha20-Poly1305 (file/chunk data) ├─► BLAKE2b-512(KDF_CONTEXT_FILENAME_SIV) ──► Filename SIV Key: BLAKE2b-512 (deterministic nonce) ├─► BLAKE2b-512(KDF_CONTEXT_FILENAME_CIPHER) ─► Filename Cipher Key: XChaCha20-Poly1305 (AEAD) └─► BLAKE2b-512(KDF_CONTEXT_IPC_AUTH) ──► IPC Auth Key: BLAKE2b-512 (challenge-response) ``` - **Context-Bound AEAD**: File payloads include `inode_id` + `chunk_idx` + `flags` in AAD; seekable chunks bind ciphertext to chunk index. - **Zeroize on Drop**: All keys implement `ZeroizeOnDrop`; password verifiers use `Zeroizing`. - **SIV Filenames**: 192-bit synthetic IV (BLAKE2b-512) provides deterministic encryption without IV storage. ### FUSE Engine — Pure-Rust Kernel Protocol [`fuse.rs`][repo://src/fuse.rs#L1-L100] implements FUSE ABI v7.28 with zero external C dependencies: | Capability | Detail | |------------|--------| | **Platforms** | Linux (`/dev/fuse` + `fusermount3`), macOS (macFUSE/osxfuse `SCM_RIGHTS`) | | **ABI Support** | Dual Linux (88B `FuseAttr`) + macOS (104B `FuseAttr` with `crtime`/`flags`) | | **Handle Table** | SeqLock 256-slot fast path + `RwLock` fallback; 1,000+ FUSE handles on 1 `.img` FD | | **Max Write Negotiation** | Dynamic: Linux `FUSE_MAX_PAGES` + `/sys/module/fuse/parameters/max_pages_limit`; macOS `-o iosize` | | **macOS Hardening** | Finder metadata storm filter (`.DS_Store`, `._*`); UTF-8 NFD→NFC normalization | | **Read-Only Enforcement** | `-EROFS` on all mutations when `read_only` mount option or `DiskManager::is_read_only()` | ### NFSv3 Server — Pure-Rust Loopback [`nfs.rs`][repo://src/nfs.rs#L1-L100] implements ONC RPC v2 / XDR / MOUNT v3 / NFS v3 over a single loopback TCP listener: | Feature | Implementation | |---------|----------------| | **File Handles** | 16-byte stateless: `[fs_generation: u64 LE, inode_id: u64 LE]` | | **Programs** | MOUNT v3 (100005) + NFS v3 (100003) multiplexed on 127.0.0.1 | | **Operations** | GETATTR, SETATTR, LOOKUP, ACCESS, **Safety** | Bounded 2 MiB frame cap; panic-free XDR codec returns clean ONC errors | ### MCP Server — AI Agent Sandbox [`oifs_mcp.rs`][repo://src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs#L1-L50] exposes OIFS as MCP tools over stdio JSON-RPC: ```json { "mcpServers": { "oifs-sandbox": { "command": "oifs_mcp", "args": ["/path/to/agent_workspace.img", "--size", "64"], "env": { "OIFS_PASSWORD": "optional-vault-password" } } } } ``` **Exposed Tools**: `read_file`, `write_file`, `append_file`, `list_dir`, `mkdir`, `delete_file`, `truncate_file`, `status`. --- ## Data Flow: Write Path (Create + Write) ```mermaid (RwLock) DiskManager->>Pipeline: plan_write_prepared() [OUT-OF-LOCK] Pipeline->>Pipeline: SIMD Filter (Delta/Shuffle/BitShuffle) Pipeline->>Pipeline: Zstd Compress (Seekable 64K / Stream) Pipeline->>Pipeline: XChaCha20-Poly1305 Encrypt (AAD = inode_id + chunk_idx + flags) Pipeline-->>DiskManager: WritePlan { case, buffer, new_size, new_compressed_size, nonce } DiskManager->>DiskManager: Allocate blocks (extent-based) DiskManager->>WAL: Stage MetadataOp (WriteInode, AllocBlocks, etc.) DiskManager->>WAL: Commit transaction (CRC32C frame + commit marker) DiskManager->>Storage: Write payload blocks (Mmap: memcpy / FileIo: pwrite) DiskManager->>Storage: Flush per DurabilityMode DiskManager-->>Client: Ok(()) ``` --- ## Cross-System Integration Points | Interface | Entry Point | Session Mode | Storage Mode | Key Types | |-----------|-------------|--------------|--------------|-----------| | **Rust API** | `DiskManager::open*` | All (via `OifsSession`) | Mmap / FileIo | `DiskManager`, `OifsAsyncTask` | | **C FFI** | `oifs_open`, `oifs_read_at` | Standalone only | Mmap / FileIo | `oifs.h`, `oifs.hpp`, `co_await` | | **FUSE** | `OifsFuseFs::mount()` | Standalone (direct) | Mmap / FileIo | `FuseMountOptions`, `OifsFuseFs` | | **NFS** | `OifsNfsServer::new().run()` | Standalone (direct) | Mmap / FileIo | `NfsMountOptions`, `OifsNfsServer` | | **CLI** | `oifs` binary | All (`--ipc`, `--network`) | Mmap / FileIo (`--no-mmap`) | `src/bin/oifs.rs` | | **MCP** | `oifs_mcp` binary | Standalone (direct) | Mmap (default) | `src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs` | **Shared Invariants**: - All frontends share the same `DiskManager` core — no forked logic. - `OifsSession::get_or_open*` provides process-wide session deduplication via
